#1994. Manchester United’s attack may be their best form of defence this season

Is attack going to be Manchester United’s best form of defence this season?

There was plenty to like going forward, particularly once United had nudged their way in front after their second lucky break of what had hitherto looked like being a tricky afternoon.

Give this team a little space and they have the attacking players to inflict some serious damage, none more so than Bruno Fernandes who, just five days after collecting the PFA Players’ Player of the Year award, scored a hat-trick in what was another inspired performance.

Ipswich Town will testify to that after a sobering second half when it felt like United were going to score with every raid forward and, for a time, even threaten to equal the nine goals they scored against the promoted side at this ground 31 years ago.

In the returning Marcus Rashford, whom manager Michael Carrick likened to a “new signing”, Matheus Cunha, Bryan Mbeumo and, of course, Fernandes, United have an intriguing blend of attacking players. Throw in Kobbie Mainoo who, on another day, would have stolen the headlines with an imperious display in central midfield, and one thing United are not lacking for is creativity.

Their offensive problems tend to come when opponents sit in and ask to be broken down. Hull City, of course, proved as much last weekend when United looked desperately short of ideas in attack.

But you would probably bet on Carrick being more likely to find solutions to that particular conundrum than some of the defensive headaches that again reared their head here.

A week after that shock 2-0 defeat to Hull, United were given another scare when Ipswich took advantage of more meek defending to lead and could easily have scored more in that first half.

With a couple of days of the transfer window still remaining, it would feel remiss of United not to add a quality left-back before the deadline passes.

Those 15 minutes in the first half when Abdul Fatawu gave Luke Shaw a torrid time, not least in that moment he raced away from the United defender to cross for Leif Davis to score, should tell United’s hierarchy everything about the risks of not reinforcing in the position.

Ipswich STUN Old Trafford! Leif Davis does superbly to volley past Senne Lammens and give Gary O'Neil's side the lead 💥 pic.twitter.com/sJ0XNf8OiT

Defensive rebuilding is next summer’s big project but some things cannot wait and that is before we get to some of the issues in the other full-back position, which Ipswich also exploited. Fatawu aside, Daizen Maeda and Davis caused Diogo Dalot and Mbeumo problems down United’s right and the excellent Julio Enciso was a persistent nuisance until the game fell away from Ipswich.

For all the defensive concerns, though, United were exhilarating going forward, especially once they found themselves in front after benefiting from a curious ruling that dictated Harry Maguire’s “accidental” handball in the lead-up to the home team’s second goal was “not punishable” because he did not end up scoring.

In other words, had Maguire himself found the net and not seen his cross-cum-shot deflect in off the Ipswich defender Jacob Greaves, the goal would not have stood.

Harry Maguire's shot cannons in off Jacob Greaves and Manchester United are in front at Old Trafford after a VAR review! 💪 pic.twitter.com/hUdogDQX6k

United were brilliant from that point on. There had been flashes of the threat they hold in the opening 45 minutes but thereafter Ipswich just found themselves routinely bludgeoned and unable to escape the tailspin. As the rain poured down, the goals poured in. Gary O’Neil, the Ipswich manager, talked about a lack of “emotional discipline” but plenty of teams would have found United hard to contain in that moment.

Rashford was a threat on his first start for United for 626 days. Harness his talent in the right way and he will be an enormous asset. Cunha’s withdrawn role, with Fernandes and Mbeumo routinely racing in behind United’s false nine, caused Ipswich no end of problems. Amad Diallo and Mason Mount were missing through injury and Benjamin Sesko, a substitute, is still working his way back to fitness after missing all of pre-season. Patrick Dorgu almost scored a couple after coming on. So Carrick has plenty of options.

Fernandes was at his irrepressible best, initially punishing poor Marcelino Núñez after his slip allowed Cunha to play in the United captain to equalise five minutes before the restart and then taking the game away from Ipswich in the second.

Bruno Fernandes equalises for Manchester United! 🔴 pic.twitter.com/CdEI1REeUD

After missing two penalties in pre-season, he made no mistake from the spot after Greaves had brought down Cunha. He then steered home a close-range finish after Mbeumo’s shot was blocked and almost lobbed the Ipswich goalkeeper Kjell Scherpen from 60 yards. His last act was to send Mbeumo through to score with a delicious lob.

"He's the prince of this place!"Bruno Fernandes completes his hat-trick 🎩 pic.twitter.com/KgLlaMcKGR

This was the first time United had scored five goals in a Premier League game since beating Leeds United five years ago and you had to go back 10 years to find the last time they had more shots in a league match.

“There was a good mixture [in attack] there,” Carrick said. “Obviously we’ve got to find the right balance and options. We can play slightly different ways across the front line and a lot of the front players can play different roles.

“It was a little bit different today playing Cunha a bit deeper, and Bryan and Marcus a little bit higher. So it’s up to us to try and get that balance right, but certainly there’s creation and there’s goals within the squad, for sure.”

There was little doubt United benefited from the return of Mainoo in midfield. Summer signing Andrey Santos was the one to make way and Mainoo in turn produced the kind of intelligent, inventive display alongside Youri Tielemans that makes you wonder how Thomas Tuchel did not give the midfielder a minute for England at this summer’s World Cup.

He recycles possession beautifully, excels in the tight spaces, has a nose for goal and an eye for a pass and a lovely ability to glide past players even though he is not quick. Ipswich could not live with him.

Asked where Mainoo could still develop, Carrick said, half in jest: “On today’s performance, not much, really. I thought he was pretty much all-around, very, very good for a first start back. I understand Bruno will get a lot of credit today, and he deserves that as well, but I thought Kobbie was immense in the middle of the pitch for us and underpinned the performance of the team.”

The Man Utd head coach told Sky Sports: “It was a good win. It was a really good win in the end. We played some really good football. The biggest thing today was the mentality of the boys tp overcomes setbacks. We’re going to have them and it depends on how you deal with them. I was really pleased with that. It’s easy to look at the result but the mentality and the stubbornness really pleased me.

“We controlled the game pretty well for the most part. A lot of our play was looking on the way to how we wanted it to look. The boys took it on really well and we were fabulous.”

And on Bruno Fernandes, Carrick added: “He showed his quality today. Bruno did what he’s good at. He’s had a big week winning awards. Three goals and a fantastic performance.

“There were a lot of positives with and without the ball but it’s the whole mentality dealing with it and trusting each other. Last week didn’t go for us and we accept that. Today was a lot better.

“We’re not getting carried away. We were down last week but everything wasn’t wrong. We can still get better, we haven’t cracked it. We’ll get ready for the next.”

Speaking with Sky Sports, he said: “Really unlucky to be 2-1 down, really unlucky - two of the most unlucky goals you will see, but then not good enough to get back into it. We got punished by a very good side.

“To beat Manchester United at Old Trafford you need the moments to go in your favour and they didn’t. Rules can go against you, or a deflection, there are lots of things that can happen in a game that are beyond your control.

“It is a complicated rule - handball if it’s the goal scorer but not if it takes a deflection and was heading off the target. I think that is tough for a referee.

“But no problem. I’m not here to moan about refs. We get no points, at Old Trafford a lot of people leave with no points but we leave with an understanding of where to get better.

“We have three points from two tough games. A good start for us. It is the Premier League, the lads understand there will be highs and lows. We don’t want there to be too many lows but the lads are fine in there. They understand.”

"I understand the rules, but it doesn't feel right" Ashley Young and Darren Bent react to the reasoning behind Harry Maguire's potential handball not being given 🎙️ pic.twitter.com/MGJdBNhbYx

"We deserved that little bit of luck"Harry Maguire discusses Manchester United's controversial second goal where he appeared to handle the ball 🗣️ pic.twitter.com/AY3vWRCxZZ

The hat-trick hero told Sky Sports: “It was a massive result for us. We lost three points last week. First game at home, the fans have been waiting for this. It’s not to make up for last week, you can’t get six points from it. Second half we were very good.

“Scoring before half-time is always important if it’s to get on top of the game or draw the game. We were in control of the game. In the second half, we were very good.

“Scoring goals is the best feeling in football. Doing a half-time at home with our fans is something I’m proud of. I hope I can do much more and help my team-mate score goals too.”

Mission accomplished, boss 👏 https://t.co/0BGBtMYg3H pic.twitter.com/dN0DayO283

Bruno Fernandes brilliance 🌟🌟🌟 pic.twitter.com/96LiCipQKk

Fernandes stars with a second-half hat-trick as Man Utd eventually cruise to an emphatic victory over newly-promoted Ipswich at Old Trafford.

Bruno Fernandes' hat-trick inspires Man Utd to their first win of the season 👏 pic.twitter.com/GNhpUwFUkV

Dorgu looks hungry for a goal as he fires a thunderbolt towards Scherpen’s near post. The Ipswich goalkeeper is up to the task and bats the shot away for a corner.

Man Utd counter as Lammens throws the ball out to Dorgu, who has acres of space to exploit. He tries to pick out Sesko with a cross, but overhits the delivery by some distance. Man Utd look like they could score every time they venture forward.

The Argentine defender won’t want to see this back again... Enciso puts Martinez under pressure and pinches the ball off him. The Ipswich playmaker then sprints towards Lammens and unselfishly slides a pass into Akpom, who slots the ball into an empty net.

There will be eight minutes of added time to end this game.

Man Utd are pushing for a sixth goal and come scarily close to it, but Dorgo’s close-range header is parried away by Scherpen.

Five-star Man Utd are ripping Ipswich apart again. He didn’t score it, but Fernandes is at the heart of this goal. The playmaker floats a delightful ball over Ipswich’s defence for Mbeumo to chase. The forward beats Scherpen to it and lobs the Ipswich goalkeeper. As the ball bounces towards the goal, it kisses the underside of the crossbar. Despite Greaves’ best efforts, he can’t stop the ball from crossing the line.

Carrick orders a triple change as the rain begins to hammer down at Old Trafford. Cunha, Mainoo and Rashford depart for Sesko, Andrey Santos and Dorgu.

Man Utd are close to a fifth goal, but Cunha is denied by Scherpen at his near post. Just before that, Rashford showcased some exceptional skill and nutmegged Diop, but he couldn’t quite get a shot away.

After a flurry of changes for Ipswich amid the chaos, they’ve switched to a back five. Nunez, Lukic and Maeda are all off, with Palacios, Ouattara and Furlong on as the replacements. For Man Utd, Dalot and Shaw are withdrawn for Yoro and Mazraoui.

Fernandes is overflowing with confidence and attempts to lob Scherpen from near the half-way line. His cheeky attempt shaves the roof of the net.

Mbeumo’s blocked effort kindly falls into Fernandes’ path and once again, the Man Utd displays unerring compsure to calmly slide the ball into the bottom corner from close range, leaving Scherpen with no chance. Man Utd are in cruise control now.

"He's the prince of this place!"Bruno Fernandes completes his hat-trick 🎩 pic.twitter.com/KgLlaMcKGR

Rashford meets a clipped cross, but on this occasion, Scherpen is there to make a strong save.

The Portuguese playmaker is the most composed man in Old Trafford. Fernandes coolly sends Scherpen the wrong way and Man Utd now have an invaluable two-goal advantage.

Bruno Fernandes makes it 3-1 to Manchester United from the spot 🎯 pic.twitter.com/vFh7moSSpb

What a nightmare couple of minutes for Ipswich. Mainoo threads a pass through to Cunha, who is cynically apprehended by Greaves’ sliding challenge. It’s all unravelled for Ipswich. It’s a stonewall penalty. Fernandes will take it.

Wave after wave of Man Utd pressure has finally paid off. Man Utd have Ipswich trapped inside their own half as Akpom attempts to chip the ball over Maguire, who blocks it. The defender strides forward and shoots. It’s heading wide, but takes a wicked deflection off Greaves to nestle in the bottom corner. The goal stands after a VAR check.

Harry Maguire's shot cannons in off Jacob Greaves and Manchester United are in front at Old Trafford after a VAR review! 💪 pic.twitter.com/hUdogDQX6k

Some confusion to clear up following the VAR check. The ball struck Maguire’s hand before he shot, but his deflected effort stands because the Man Utd defender wasn’t deemed the ‘immediate goalscorer’ given Greaves’ intervention.

#MUNIPS – 56'The referee's call of goal for Manchester United was checked and confirmed by VAR – with it deemed that Maguire was not the immediate goalscorer after an accidental handball.VAR: "It's an own goal and the accidental handball is not punishable, so we recommend you…

When it’s not your day ... Mbeumo struggled badly offensively and defensively today and that miss from point blank range summed up his afternoon. Plenty of time yet to turn it around of course but he’s got to step it up.

How has that not gone in?! Dalot whips a deep delivery into the box and Rashford does magnificently to keep it in play, volleying the ball back across goal out of Scherpen’s reach. Mbeumo is about a metre from the goal-line and directs Rashford’s assist onto the bar. It’s an extraordinary miss.

"HOW has he missed?!" Bryan Mbeumo misses a golden opportunity to put Man Utd in front 😬 pic.twitter.com/bnZZswysJa

Enciso skips away from Mainoo and drives at Man Utd’s defence. From incredibly far out, he tries his luck, but fires his shot over the bar. Enciso has been a joy to watch so far today.

Enciso showcases some exquisite skill, pirouetting away from Cunha, who brings down the Ipswich playmaker.

We are back under way for the second half. Man Utd are unchanged at the break, while Ipswich have made an alteration, with Akpom on for Emersonn.

Ipswich have looked very useful going forward and richly deserved their opening goal. Fatawu’s dazzling run was rewarded by Davis’ composed finish, but the visitors’ lead didn’t last long. Nunez’s slip proved costly, with Cunha and Fernandes combining to devastating effect, hauling Man Utd level.

A frantic first half comes to a close. It’s been a thoroughly entertaining game of football so far, with Davis and Fernandes both netting via top-quality finishes.

End-to-end stuff at Old Trafford 🤯Leif Davies got the opening goal for Ipswich before Bruno Fernandes equalised for Man Utd. pic.twitter.com/6TAer5eiGJ

There will be two added minutes at the end of this half. Man Utd are pushing for another goal. Can they find a second before the break?

A timely bit of good fortune for United. Cunha takes advantage of poor Nunez’s slip to play an inch perfect pass in behind for the rampaging Fernandes to race clear and fire home.

Disaster for Nunez... Ipswich have a lot of players up the pitch following a long throw-in and the ball is played back to Nunez. The midfielder slips, gifting the hosts a counter attack. Cunha pounces and slides an inch-perfect pass through to the onrushing Fernandes. The Man Utd captain then fires a thunderous effort in at Scherpen’s near post. It’s a magnificent strike. The Ipswich goalkeeper has no chance of saving that. Nunez looks absolutely gutted.

Bruno Fernandes equalises for Manchester United! 🔴 pic.twitter.com/CdEI1REeUD

Fatawu receives a yellow card for clattering into Mbeumo. This game is being played at breakneck speed.

You would have expected Man Utd to come bursting out of the blocks following last week’s disappointment against Hull, but it’s been a really underwhelming display from the hosts so far. Ipswich deserve their lead.

Ipswich nearly make it two! It’s the same combination for Ipswich as Fatawu floats a deep cross into the box for Davis, who makes a late run. Davis meets the delivery from close range, but doesn’t get a clean connection on the strike, allowing Lammens to tip his effort over the bar.

If the first half an hour or so here has done anything, it’s underline how much United need upgrades and reinforcements at full-back. United are in the market for a left back before the window closes and the way Shaw jumped in and then was done by Fatawu for the goal may see those efforts intensified. Davis was criminally unmarked in the middle (what a finish, though, allowing the ball to come across his body then side foot in) with Mbeumo nowhere.

And United haven’t learned from it. Moments later and Fatawu clips in a cross - with not nearly enough pressure from Shaw to shut it out - and Davis is again unmarked at the back with Dalot occupied and Mbeumo ball watching. United are having a real wobble here. Ipswich have been superb. Gary O’Neil will be loving what he is seeing from his side - they’re brave, aggressive and playing with pace and lots of incisive movement.

What a goal from Davis! Fatawu nutmegs Shaw and then outpaces the Man Utd defender. He reaches the byline and picks out the arriving Davis with a pinpoint. Ipswich’s left back then applies a superb finish, directing a superb half-volley in off the bar.

Ipswich STUN Old Trafford! Leif Davis does superbly to volley past Senne Lammens and give Gary O'Neil's side the lead 💥 pic.twitter.com/sJ0XNf8OiT

Mbeumo floats a deep cross towards Rashford at the back post. The Englishman reaches it, but given the power on the delivery, he can’t quite keep it in play.

Man Utd win another free-kick in presentable territory. On this occasion, Fernandes curls his strike into the Ipswich wall.

Davis threads a clever pass trough to Maeda, who creeps in behind Dalot. The winger bursts into the penalty area, before arrowing a powerful attempt towards the far post, but Lammens is there to make a pivotal stop. Ipswich have looked dangerous going forward.

There’s space in behind Diogo Dalot that Ipswich have again exploited, this time with a fine Leif Davis ball for Daizen Maeda to surge in behind the United right back and force a second big save from Lammens. United look a threat going forward but then so do Ipswich, who are picking their moments to break and doing so well.

Rashford tries his luck from long range with a knuckle-ball free-kick. He doesn’t get any accuracy on the strike and it harmlessly flies off target.

This game has exploded into life in the last couple of minutes. End to end action. Scherpen first denying Dalot, then Ipswich going straight down the other end from a long punted clearance and Enciso, holding off Shaw and Mbeumo, forcing a save from Lammens. In keeping with the basketball nature of things, United then went back up the other end, with Cunha overhitting a cross for the onrushing Rashford before Fernandes’ goalbound shot is blocked. It’s certainly entertaining.

Chances at both ends! Firstly, Emersonn hacks Man Utd’s corner away, and Enciso uses his blistering speed to outpace Shaw and Mbeumo, creating a one-on-one with Lammens, who does excellently to smother the shot. Then Man Utd then fly forward straight away and Cunha fires a low delivery across the six-yard box which is marginally out of Rashford’s reach.

Man Utd counter as Fernandes releases Mbeumo with a ball over the top. The hosts recycle the ball well after Rashford crosses, allowing Dalot to cut in or his left foot and bend a curler for the far corner. Scherpen uses every inch of his towering frame to make an eye-catching diving save.

Maeda shows a great turn of pace to breeze past Mbeumo and reach the byline. Under pressure from Dalot, the winger hits his near post cross into Lammens’ hands.

Again, Rashford runs at Ipswich’s backline and cuts inside to reach the penalty area. He tees up Cunha, who smashes an effort well over the bar.

Martinez attempts an ambitious switch of play, aiming for Maguire, but boots the ball straight out of play. O’Shea and Shaw then both go up for a header, with the Ipswich man coming off worse and staying on the ground. He’s back on his feet now and play resumes.

There’s an early roar from the Old Trafford crowd as Rashford gets on the ball and sprints at Ipswich captain O’Shea, who is playing at right back.

Old Trafford welcomes both sides. Can Man Utd find their first win of the Premier League season or will Ipswich spoil the party?

Carlos Baleba has walking out on to the pitch after being introduced at Old Trafford. The new £70m signing from Brighton has been posing for pictures with a shirt and applauding all sections of the ground. He won’t be in action for another two or three weeks most likely owing to an existing ankle injury.

Carlos Baleba is introduced to the Manchester United fans! 👋 pic.twitter.com/QHTCkpe5dz

With kick-off fast approaching, here’s a recap of both line-ups.

Man Utd: Lammens, Dalot, Maguire, Martinez, Shaw, Mainoo, Tielemans, Mbeumo, Fernandes, Rashford, Cunha.

Subs: Darlow, Mazraoui, Zirkzee, Dorgu, Yoro, Santos, Heaven, Sesko, Lacey.

Ipswich: Scherpen, O’Shea, Diop, Greaves, Davis, Nunez, Lukic, Fatawu, Enciso, Maeda, Emersonn.

Subs: Walton, Furlong, Kipre, Walle, McAteer, Palacios, Akpom, Ouattara, Clarke.

"He's a fantastic footballer." Ashley Young discusses Marcus Rashford 🔊 pic.twitter.com/4hYAtx9zZF

Michael Carrick explains the changes to his Man Utd starting XI to face Ipswich 🔴Watch the game live: https://t.co/0AejI4B8dF pic.twitter.com/p9FD36h3OM

Against Hull, Man Utd’s forward line looked way off the pace. In an attempt to stop history repeating itself, Michael Carrick has turned to Marcus Rashford, who is making his first start for the club since the end of 2024.

When Rashford last featured for Man Utd, he was wearing the No.10 shirt. That is now occupied by Mathues Cunha who starts as the central frontman, with Rashford now sporting the No.9.

The hosts will also need captain Bruno Fernandes to deliver. He will levels below his exceptionally high standards last time out, while Bryan Mbeumo also needs to make more of an impact.

It was short and not sweet. Playing in their first top-flight campaign since 2001-02, Ipswich finished 19th with just 22 points under Kieran McKenna.

This time, Gary O’Neil is the boss and they’ve already ticked off one victory thanks to those three points against Sunderland.

Is he the man to guide Ipswich to safety?

Martinez and Dalot are two alterations in Man Utd’s backline, replacing Ayden Heaven and Noussair Mazraoui. Gary Neville feels the club’s defence could let them down this season.

"You can get at them" ❌Gary Neville has concerns over Manchester United's defence for the upcoming season particularly after defeat to Hull 🤔 pic.twitter.com/v3sEjInI2j

First game of the season at Old Trafford for United and one they really need to win after last weekend’s shock defeat at newly promoted Hull City.

Summer signing Andrey Santos has made way for Kobbie Mainoo to partner Youri Tielemans in attack and it’ll be really interesting to see how that midfield pairing dovetail.

It’s a first start at Old Trafford since December 2024 for Marcus Rashford in an attacking looking side. Matheus Cunha is likely to operate as a false nine.

There’s going to be an onus on Rashford and Bryan Mbeumo to provide pace and penetration from out wide and get in behind Ipswich’s defence.

Ipswich enjoyed a great start back in the top flight by winning their opening game against Sunderland and will be out to build on that victory.

Against Hull, Michael Carrick opted for a midfield pivot of Man Utd debutants Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans. However, the pair were completely overran by Hull’s intensity and energy.

Carrick has turned to Kobbie Mainoo as the resolution, with the 21-year-old replacing Andrey Santos. Mainoo went to the World Cup with England this summer, but didn’t play a single minute.

A return to Old Trafford will give Mainoo a chance to remind everyone of his quality.

"I wouldn't say massive concerns, but he will be worried""If Carrick doesn't see a reaction today, there is a problem"The Manchester United players will be under pressure to perform, says Ashley Young 📈 pic.twitter.com/dR6uat4l2P

Man Utd: Lammens, Dalot, Maguire, Martinez, Shaw, Mainoo, Tielemans, Mbeumo, Fernandes, Rashford, Cunha.

Subs: Darlow, Mazraoui, Zirkzee, Dorgu, Yoro, Santos, Heaven, Sesko, Lacey.

Ipswich: Scherpen, O’Shea, Diop, Greaves, Davis, Nunez, Lukic, Fatawu, Enciso, Maeda, Emersonn.

Subs: Walton, Furlong, Kipre, Walle, McAteer, Palacios, Akpom, Ouattara, Clarke.

Gary O’Neil has named an unchanged line-up from the side that beat Sunderland last week. Recent signing Exequiel Palacios is on the bench after joining from Bayer Leverkusen.

Your Town at Old Trafford! ✊ pic.twitter.com/mVMj2LVNvs

Unsurprisingly, Michael Carrick has shuffled his pack after last weekend’s disastrous defeat to Hull. Rashford, Mainoo, Martinez and Dalot all come into the starting X1.

📍 Home.Back where we belong. https://t.co/VbvwRcdF4t pic.twitter.com/37rThnGjyN

Good afternoon and welcome to our live coverage of Sunday’s late Premier League kick-off between Manchester United and Ipswich Town at Old Trafford.

Man Utd suffered an almighty upset last weekend as they slumped to a shock 2-0 defeat against Hull City in Yorkshire. The hosts scored twice after 38 minutes, leaving Michael Carrick’s men with a mountain to climb, but they simply had no answer so Man Utd were shambolic defensively and toothless in attack.

When the fixture list was released, everyone looked at Man Utd’s opening two games against newly-promoted sides as the ideal opportunity for maximum points. But now, there is serious pressure on today’s home team to deliver in front of their fans.

Reflecting on last week’s loss in a press conference ahead of this outing, Carrick said: “I think your success comes from how well you deal with setbacks in the end. In any position, or certainly any sport, particularly this one, going through a season, there are going to be setbacks, sometimes a bit smaller than others. It’s how you deal with that initially, how you react to it and what comes next. I think that ultimately decides what type of team you’re going to become.

“So far, we’ve dealt with those setbacks really well within games and game to game. We had one last week, there’s no getting away from it, and it’s disappointing, but we’re looking to bounce back. We’ve had a good week. The boys have re-focused, learnt from where we could have improved and kept pushing forward.”

Against the odds, Ipswich began their 2026-27 Premier League campaign with a 2-1 comeback victory over Sunderland, with summer signing Emersonn equalising before substitute Jack Clarke found a 90th-minute winner at Portman Road. They followed this game with another triumph at home in midweek, beating Leicester City 3-1 in the League Cup second round.

With all eyes on Man Utd after their stuttering start, Ipswich will see this as an ideal opportunity to ruffle the feathers of a Premier League heavyweight and further dent their sky-high ambitions.

Kick-off is at 16:30, with team news coming shortly.

#1992. Ex-Rangers star signs for new club in second tier after weeks as free agent

Former Rangers midfielder Greg Docherty has signed for Preston North End as a free agent.

The 30-year-old has been without a club since leaving Charlton Athletic by mutual agreement near the end of the summer transfer window, despite having captained them to promotion from League One a year before.

With the Addicks continually strengthening for the Championship, he found himself out of favour and it was agreed he could move on in search of first team football.

Former Motherwell boss Graham Alexander recently took over at Preston and was tipped in recent weeks to make a move for Docherty, after admitting he was looking at free agents. That has now come to fruition.

Preston announced the signing today and Docherty told their website: “I’m really proud to be here, to have this badge on my chest and to be part of a club that’s steeped in history. When I told my family, they were all excited and willing me to get it done.

“I’m just thankful that we managed to do it. Coming down from Scotland and playing in England, Preston’s a very good team to get to for my family and I’ve always kept an eye on them.

Derek McInnes news, interviews and updates on the Rangers manager The quietly effective Rangers star McInnes says inspires dressing-room confidence

“I’ve always loved playing at Deepdale but haven’t won very often there, so hopefully that will change now. When I was an opposition player, I always found it really difficult. I’ve got family in the north of England and this move just really ticks all the boxes.

“To be a Preston player is something I’ve always wanted to do and I’m really proud to have finally done it.”

Docherty has been training with Alexander's side already and added: “From the moment I walked in here, I got a really good feeling from speaking to the manager and all the coaching staff.

“When I see how passionate the manager is about turning our current situation around, it excites me and I want to also help change things. I see real quality in the dressing room and I know we can improve if we keep working hard.

“The manager’s training demands are very high, and I’ve come in and really enjoyed it. I’ve enjoyed the soreness after it, I’ve enjoyed the tiredness after it, but I feel much better for it and all the lads do too.

“The boys are saying they’re getting fitter, which is massive in this league, and I just can’t wait to get going alongside them out on the pitch.”

Alexander said: “We’re really pleased to bring Greg in. He’s been a captain, won promotions and knows the game inside out.

“Greg’s vocal, fit and motivated, which are all the key things you look for in a professional footballer.

“He has settled into the group really quickly and has a real willingness to show what he can do.”

#1990. The Celtic star who is 'absolute saviour' and teammate full of 'magic'

Joe Hart has branded Camilo Duran an "absolute saviour" for Celtic, and Callum Osmand a player with a "magic moment" in his locker.

The former Parkhead goalkeeper now watches on as a fan and was delighted to see his old club get their mojo back with a win over Besiktas - a first victory in this year's Europa League.

Hart has been taking a closer look at the domestic form and insists Celtic are not doing any worse than in previous title-winning campaigns.

And he has picked out Duran and Osmand as two matchwinners in the side.

The turning point that inspired Celtic to big European victory against Besiktas How Celtic trio fared in B Team defeat to Ross County as O'Neill watches on

"That’s the thing about that club, and that is why I adore it, and I’m so pleased that I got to spend time there and be a part of it. The expectancy and the expectation, unless you are a Celtic man or a Celtic person, you wouldn’t understand, because, like you say, they’re still top," the Englishman told the Overlap Daily.

"I think Rangers have a game in hand because they played in a cup semi-final at the weekend, but even if they win that, they’re still a point behind. And domestically, Celtic have lost two and drawn one in 11 games. It’s not the reason. I was looking at how they’ve started leagues in the past eight, nine years, and they’re right up there with what they do, but they’re not flowing. The strikers aren’t scoring.

"Camilo Durán has been an absolute saviour this season. Him and Callum Osmand came on, I think, around the 60th minute, with it looking ominous, 1-0 down against Besiktas, who were flying high, a good team.

"And Callum Osmand’s first touch, he smashed it through bodies. He’s got that magic moment in him. He had it last year. He’s the one who scored when they beat Heart of Midlothian 3-1, and he got to run the length of the field on his own. He scored a couple of big goals in the title run-in as well.

"But it made me happy to feel the stadium shake through the TV, because that stadium does go wild, and people are talking with their feet. It wasn’t a sold-out crowd, which is so unlike Celtic.”

By Darren Plant | 05 Nov 2026 16:11

Newport County and Walsall square off in the FA Cup first round on Saturday afternoon.

These two teams play in the fourth tier of English football, sitting in 14th and third position in the League Two table respectively.

Having signed a long-term contract with Walsall, Lee Grant will get time to secure promotion to League One.

However, the Saddlers entered November having lost just one of 13 games in League Two, that defeat coming by a 4-2 scoreline to runaway leaders Salford City.

Walsall have conceded just eight goals in their other 12 league games, while they bounced back from the Salford disappointment by beating Colchester United last time out.

Sitting in third place with a game in hand on the teams below them, Grant will be delighted with the progression of his team.

Only once in eight years - the 2020-21 coronavirus-hit campaign - have Walsall failed to reach the second round of the FA Cup.

Just as impressively, Newport have only not progressed to the second round of the competition on two occasions in 11 years.

After consecutive near-misses with relegation to the National League, Newport have 18 points from their opening 14 games in 2026-27.

Hayden Mullins has brought some much-needed stability to the club, losing just four times across the aforementioned period.

Although Walsall are yet to suffer a league away defeat, Newport have not lost in seven League Two fixtures at Rodney Parade.

This tie was drawn out in the first round of the 2016-17 FA Cup, Newport prevailing by a 2-1 scoreline on that occasion.

Having been able to make changes in the EFL Trophy in midweek, Mullins may stick with a similar Newport XI from the 4-1 win over Chesterfield last weekend.

Harrison Biggins played a key role with a goal and an assist, taking him to seven such contributions in League Two during 2026-27.

Shaquille Gwengwe is available again after serving a three-match ban for an incident in the fixture with York City on October 17.

Ryan Leak, James Furlong, Sven Sprangler, Courtney Clarke and Andy Dallas could all return to the Walsall XI, with Grant likely to want to freshen up his team.

Declan Skura, Mason Hancock, Isaac Moore, Reece Smith and Aaron Pressley - five players who have accumulated a lot of game time in League Two - could drop down to the substitutes' bench.

#1988. Nicky Butt tears into 'bluffer' and 'cheat' Lisandro Martinez after his red card against Chelsea - and insists he should be the first player on Man United's chopping block in January

By HARRY BAMFORTH, LIVE SPORTS COVERAGE REPORTER

Published: 15:53 EDT, 2 November 2026 | Updated: 03:05 EDT, 3 November 2026

Former Manchester United midfielder Nicky Butt has ripped into Lisandro Martinez following the defender's red card at Chelsea on Saturday.

The United centre-back was given his marching orders in the second half of the 2-0 defeat at Stamford Bridge for picking up two yellow cards in the space of 82 seconds.

The second of those cards came when Martinez flung an arm into the face of Wesley Fofana in the penalty box with the crucial game hanging in the balance. Cole Palmer ultimately squeezed the spot kick past Senne Lammens to secure three points for the Blues.

Martinez has been solely blamed by many for the defeat and Nicky Butt, who has previously criticised the Argentine, ripped into the 28-year-old on Piers Morgan's show Football Uncensored, dubbing him a 'cheat' for elbowing Fofana.

'Performance-wise, he's been lacking so much,' Butt said. 'And again, I was never the best player. I know my level, I know I had a lot of bad games, but one thing I did every time I went out was run myself into the ground. He threw it in the other day.

'He threw it in with that elbow because that was the most obvious thing anybody could do. And the reason he did it is because he's not strong enough to defend properly.'

Nicky Butt has hit out at Man United defender Lisandro Martinez for getting sent off at Chelsea

Butt called Martinez a 'bluffer' and a 'cheat' during a near three-minute-rant on the player

Martinez has hit the headlines more than once in the last month after he hit out at United's Director of Football Jason Wilcox for the club's lack of business, following a 2-0 defeat to Atletico Madrid in the Champions League.

However, Butt, who was a part of United's famous 1999 treble-winning team, has claimed that if Martinez made those comments as part of former squads, he would have come in for harsh treatment.

'He has got the audacity to go out onto an interview and s**g off the powers that be about buying players when he is not even playing well himself. And if they were going to spend money on players, he'd [ought to] be careful because he's the first one they'd replace.'

He added: 'If it was back in my day, he would have completely had his head ripped off. Everyone would have said, "Who do you think you are talking about me like that with the performances you're putting in?". And even if you're European Player of the Year, you still don't talk like that about your team-mates.

'He has now gone from - I have no idea why - someone that the fans loved to someone the fans loathe and want out of their football club.'

It is not the first time Butt has had his say on Martinez, with the pair embroiled in a feud earlier this year. Back in January, Martinez hit back at comments made by Paul Scholes and Butt mocking his size, and dared the former United duo to repeat them to his face.

Martinez was given his marching orders and conceded a penalty after striking Wesley Fofana's face during a 2-0 defeat at Stamford Bridge

The Argentine told them they can come 'to my house' and 11 months on Butt started his near-three-minute rant by referencing the back and forth.

'That lad's a bluffer, full stop,' Butt said. The Butcher his nickname is. With him, he called out my mate; it was probably my fault because I said something tongue-in-cheek on a podcast.

'It was like, "Haaland would pick up and carry him". It was tongue-in-cheek, even though Solanke did it one week ago.

'He's come out and called out a player who has won 11 Premier Leagues for Manchester United, and played for god knows how many years, about you come and see me and knock on my front door.

'You can't say anything about these players because they get all touchy with it.'

#1987. Next Man Utd manager: Red Devils make Didier Deschamps 'move' amid Michael Carrick sack talk

By Carter White | 05 Nov 2026 16:25, Last updated: 05 Nov 2026 20:48

Manchester United have reportedly made contact with Didier Deschamps over potentially taking charge from Michael Carrick as head coach.

The former Red Devils midfielder is under extreme pressure at Old Trafford following an awful domestic start to the campaign, with the 20-time English champions currently sitting in 17th spot in the Premier League table.

Despite being level on points with the top-flight relegation zone after nine matches, Man Utd produced a marvellous comeback on the continental scene earlier in the week, beating Italian giants Roma 3-2 at the Theatre of Dreams.

The Red Devils have been heavily linked to Europa League specialist Unai Emery in recent weeks, however, Aston Villa are supposedly closing in on a contract agreement for the Spaniard.

One of the top-performing bosses in European football at the moment, Cesc Fabregas of Como recently masterminded a 9-1 battering of Lens in the League Phase of the Champions League on Wednesday night.

According to French publication Footmercato, Manchester United have added another high-profile name to their shortlist of possible managerial replacements for Carrick, who is walking on thin ice at Old Trafford.

The Red Devils have supposedly made initial contact with former France manager Deschamps, who has been out of work since taking Les Bleus to the semi-finals of the 2026 World Cup in North America.

The report states that the 58-year-old is not particularly keen on a switch to the Theatre of Dreams given the club's current predicament, however, a deal between the two parties cannot be ruled out.

It is understood that Man Utd have also touched base with Aston Villa hero Emery and ex-Germany and Bayern Munich head coach Julian Nagelsmann, with Carrick potentially one poor result away from the sack.

After departing his French post in July, it is believed that Deschamps was under consideration for the vacant position at Real Madrid before Los Blancos decided to reunite with Jose Mourinho.

To a certain extent, Didier Deschamps was the final evolution of Gareth Southgate on the international scene, receiving plenty of criticism during his long reign but ultimately lifting titles - something that his English counterpart failed to do.

The 58-year-old managed superstars such as Paul Pogba, N'Golo Kante, Olivier Giroud and Kylian Mbappe to success at the 2018 World Cup in Russia, where Luka Modric's Croatia were beaten in the final.

After that, a 2021 UEFA Nations League title did little to address the clamour for further major trophies in France, with Deschamps's side failing to lift the 2026 World Cup despite possessing arguably the best starting XI at the tournament.

#1986. Why Celtic bench heroes did not start against Besiktas as Martin O'Neill explains decision-making

Celtic manager Martin O'Neill made no apologies for keeping his Europa League heroes in reserve - revealing it was always the plan to unleash goalscorers Camilo Duran and Callum Osman on Besiktas at the hour mark.

Duran netted twice and Osmand also popped up with a goal as Celtic defeated Besiktas 3-2 in Glasgow to breathe life into their Europa League campaign.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Celtic needed a victory after three opening losses in the competition and now sit 32nd in the standings. O'Neill believes the win over what he labelled "a fine Besiktas side" gives them a chance of progression to the knockout stages.

The 74-year-old rotated his team due to fatigue and a heavy schedule, and deserved praise for bringing on Duran and Osmand - his most dynamic forwards - when the game became open.

"I'm not standing up for myself, absolutely not, not at all," said O'Neill. "It was designed to do exactly what it did. We have been playing Sunday, Thursday, Sunday, Thursday, Wednesday, whatever day it happens to be. We have played, I don't know what, nine games in 23 days or 24 days.

"Some players need a little breather, and you can get re-energised from coming on the field. I'm going to say that this was exactly our plan, and those players who came on, were going to come on, at some stage or another in the game."

O'Neill urged his Celtic team to build on the victory both in the Premiership and in Europe, with Kilmarnock visiting Parkhead on Sunday. He also hailed the character of his players for recovering from the concession of the opener and then a late leveller.

"We've given ourselves a chance because of the result," continued O'Neill. "The game was quite difficult but we came through it. We came through with flying colours.

"They were really, really terrific. We could have caved in. We were doing fine after the penalty goes in but we came roaring back. They all played their parts, obviously, in a big, big manner. But it was everything that we'd shown, I think, and it might just give us a sort of a platform to charge on.

"It's not going to be easy but at least we can park the European events for a few weeks' time but this definitely gives us a chance. That's what it does.

"In every aspect I thought we played some really lovely stuff as well too and they are a very fine side, there's no question about it. Very fine team. But, as you say, the character shone through in the side, no question about that. Some of these lads who have been at the football club for some time, who have been big winners at the football club, I thought they came to the fore. And also some of the lads who joined us, big performances."

Duran was the hero once again, with his goal tally now at 13, and O'Neill said of his talisman: "If you're talking about knowing your best side, he'll be in the side. He looked a wee bit tired in the last couple of games. Totally expected to be. It's been really tough. A lot of games that these lads are playing. But he's class player. Class player."

#1985. Nelson wants Lewes to fire again after missing bonfire week spark

In a tough pair of fixtures, Nelson’s side welcomed play-off-pushing Wingate & Finchley and Dartford to The Dripping Pan and netted three goals across the games.

They ended with a 2-2 draw with the North Londoners and a 2-1 defeat to their Kent visitors, however, and will reflect on two entertaining games where they lacked the fine margins.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

Following the midweek defeat to Dartford, Nelson said: “I think we fashioned chances, but in those chances, we've got to take one at least.

“I can't keep standing in front of you and saying that we've had so many chances, but we end up with a low goal ratio.”

In the defeat to Ben Greenhalgh’s Dartford side, Lewes were punished by a seven-minute double from the visitors and had too little time to draw level after Brian Garzon’s 82nd-minute goal.

There were several decent chances, but in the face of a sturdy Darts defence, the Rooks fell just short.

As the Kent side look to build on a 6th-place finish last season and secure a return to the National League South, it was a useful marker of where Lewes stand with a third of the league season gone.

“I think they didn't have many chances in the game to warrant the win based on our second half performance,” said Nelson.

“But credit to them; they've come here, done what they needed to do, and in the end, we couldn't break them down.

“You don't win games of football by having ‘nearly’ chances. They were the ones that took their chances. But I think on the balance of the game, we did enough to get something from it.”

The story was similar last Saturday, when Lewes led Wingate & Finchley through a 14th-minute Charlie Walker free-kick but let the visitors back in through a scrappy couple of goals before half-time.

A well-worked short corner just two minutes into the second half saw Enkh notch the crucial equaliser, but an end-to-end second half saw neither side net a winner.

Lewes dropped one place in the table over the weekend, with Eastbourne Borough leapfrogging them into 3rd, and they will be conscious about how the table is now contracting.

Nelson urged his players to move on quickly, saying: “Don't feel sorry for yourself. We haven't got the time for that. We've got two back-to-back hard games again with Dulwich away, and then Enfield in the week; they're not going to feel sorry for us.

“Sometimes you need a little bit of a reality check.”

The Rooks head to Dulwich Hamlet this Saturday, with a 3pm kick-off at Champion Hill.

#1984. From Hibs casual to a sold-out Hydro - the incredible story of bare-knuckle boxing's Leith Warrior

The hands might tell a story although Lewis Knox will hope they know when to stop blabbing. After all, he doesn't want his tools of the trade to betray him.

These fists helped him survive on Leith’s mean streets. As a former Hibs casual, he once used them to defend his club’s honour.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

In a more legitimate context, one less likely to interest the authorities, they are crucial for his current job installing sofas up and down the country. And more pressingly, in Glasgow on Saturday, these hands will be used as weapons with the aim of drawing blood.

“All legal and above board,” Knox clarifies. Welcome to the world of “BKFC”, which stands for Bare Knuckle Fighting Championship. The promotion, co-owned by controversial UFC star Conor McGregor, hits Scotland for the first time this weekend.

Only the All Blacks’ visit to Murrayfield, Celtic v Kilmarnock and possibly Aberdeen v Hibs will attract a bigger crowd in a sporting context.

Still, it’s guaranteed none of those involved in these fixtures will have spent the start of this week lugging sofas up and down stairwells. “I install them into houses from Berwick-Upon-Tweed to near enough Stonehaven," says Knox. "12-hour shifts, 7 am to 7 pm. Four days on, four days off. But I am still training every night. As well as being a dad of three."

Even the All Blacks, who have been utilising the gym where Knox has been training under the watchful eye of Ali Thomson, might wince at the thought of this schedule. Thomson describes Knox as a "phenomenon". He complains his own arms are aching from doing pads with the focused fighter in the run-up to this weekend.

"People say things are impossible,” ponders Knox. “But you know if you really want it? Things can be done. My mum, my dad, my family. They all support me. Everyone is tuned into it. They all try to help out. This is not an overnight thing, this has been three years in the making to get to where I am now. I have worked so hard."

He was in Fife as recently as Monday delivering sofas but who knows where he will be this time next year? The bare-knuckle scene is taking off, boosted by McGregor's involvement. "I'd like to turn pro," says Knox, 29. Remember that Hearts fan ridiculed for claiming on camera that he’d be willing to have his hands chopped off if it meant his team winning the league?

Knox loves Hibs. He was thrilled by last weekend’s League Cup semi-final win over Hearts at Hampden, which he watched on TV because he was deep in fight camp. However, he can’t afford to strike any bargain involving the prospect of losing his hands. As a bare-knuckle boxer on the cusp of his biggest ever fight, they are, after his three children, among the most precious things on earth to him.

Perhaps a little Atrixo might be in order. They are battered, bruised and a little disfigured. Hardly surprising really, since they are used to pound his opponents. “Bone on bone,” he says. “There is nothing more raw.” He reports that he hasn't broken his hands in his last three fights. "They are solid, like sledgehammers," he says.

Rather than slathering them with hand cream, Knox is considering the old fighters’ trick of sticking his hands into a bucket of sand – or rice. “It strengthens up the skin,” he says.

He broke two knuckles in his very first (official) bare-knuckle fight three years ago this month. Slightly horrifyingly, these knuckles now appear to have disappeared completely. “Yeah, disintegrated,” he says. “Two knuckles have gone, one has dipped (into the hand). As for my pinkie, I can’t stretch it out."

Knox demonstrates this inability to extend his little finger in the café where we are sitting. The Leith Warrior, as he’s known, has ordered a flat white with a shot of caramel (there was still plenty of time to make the required fighting weight of 66 kgs). If not for the damage to his hands, he seems incredibly unwarrior-like.

Softly spoken and trim, almost delicate-looking, the tattoos extending past his collar line on his neck are perhaps the main evidence of a life lived on the edge.

“I always wanted tattoos,” he says. As one suspects is the case with many people, he first succumbed to the needle and ink on holiday in Magaluf.

“A star on my chest and a Hibs tattoo on the back of my calf,” he says. “I thought I had to get serious ones after that. Ones devoted to my gran and my grandad, who both played huge parts in my life from a young age. I also have a gladiator on my arm and neck tattoos…It has become part of the job!”

As for the colours he sports when competing in the circular four-rope ring, which is designed to encourage fast-paced bouts, it wasn’t up for discussion. “Green and white, I always represent where I am from,” he says. “And a Hibs badge on my shorts. I am never not representing Leith.

“I grew up in Leith, a lot of gang culture, an environment of violence as a young boy,” he continues. “You had to be streetwise from a young age I suppose. Leith has its good and bad sides. For me, it’s one of the best places in the world. But it can be one of the worst places in the world.

"Knife crime, drugs. It’s a mix of cultures, backgrounds. I grew up in all of that. But I was never ultra-violent.”

His mother, Niki, once ran the Junction bar. Knox enjoys an obvious status in the area. A taxi driver beeps his horn as soon as he steps out of the door of our meeting place on Easter Road. Cross Knoxy and you cross Leith.

He knows people, Irvine Welsh included. The author – a more than decent boxer himself - has been mentoring Knox before his featherweight division fight against Tommy “Chaos” Carus from Liverpool at the OVO Hydro on Saturday night. Welsh has already featured in an Instagram video promoting Knox’s fight, playing the role of his manager.

“Oi, Knoxy!” he calls out after taking a phone call. “Get your dancing shoes on! We’ve got ourselves a pagger.”

Knox v Carus, or the Leith Warrior v Chaos, or indeed Scotland v England, is the third fight of 11 on a bill topped by Sean Weir’s light heavyweight title bout with Leigh Cohoon, a late stand-in for Irishman Conor ‘Da Crook’ Cooke.

Cooke’s team cited concerns about the venue layout and ticketing arrangements for their withdrawal. Some have interpreted this as another way of saying they were worried sectarian/football-related hooliganism – Weir was once a member of the Rangers Riot Crew casuals group - could flare.

Almost 11,000 are expected to converge on the Hydro for the event. BKFC is dedicated to “fighter safety”. According to their official bumph, the organisation prides itself in being “the truest form of bare-knuckle fighting”. Fighters are not allowed to wrap their hands to within one inch of the knuckle. This weekend’s spectacle is the first legally sanctioned and regulated bare knuckle event in Scotland.

For the uninitiated, the fights last for five two-minute rounds. If there isn’t a knockout, it tends to be fairly obvious who’s won.

“Cuts,” says Knox. “It comes down to facial damage. Because in boxing or any gloved fight, you can punch them ten times with a glove and not make a mark, you can punch them once with a bare knuckle and split someone’s head open.

“It is about getting as much of that in in a short period of time. The first punch usually sets the tone for the fight. It depends on where you catch him, I suppose. It is all about just getting in there and being horrible.”

It’s easy to question the ethics of unpadded pugilism. However, defenders of this ancient and previously underground practice insist it’s a safer, more honest form of boxing. "It is better for the brain, much better," claims Knox. "In boxing you get the double shock with the glove – boom, boom. It rattles the brain. You don’t see the damage facially necessarily. With bare knuckle, bone is hitting bone. That’s it. The facial damage will be shown. Internally your brain is not getting rattled for 12 rounds.

“It is five rounds of two minutes. If you last that, although you might get a few cuts, your brain is fine. To me, my brain feels fine! In my 50s and 60s I will still have a functional brain. I might have a few scars and a few missing teeth but I move pretty well (to avoid the punches). My nose is still straight...”

Inside the ring might be a veritable haven as the evening hots up on Saturday. “It is like any combat sport,” says Knox. “The crowd can be unpredictable. A bit like a football crowd. I just hope that because this event is so big for Scotland and so big for the bare-knuckle scene and for lads like myself that nothing serious kicks off. There will be some ‘characters’ there, you always get the odd person. You get that anywhere.”

Knox anticipates an unholy commotion when the first bars of Born Slippy strike up. The Underworld track is his walk on song, unsurprisingly given the Trainspotting connotations. Sunshine on Leith just wouldn’t do it in this context. Fine for after last weekend’s win for Hibs at Hampden against Hearts, but perhaps a little too plaintive, a little too pretty, for a night of good-to-honest testosterone-fuelled violence.

As much as the Easter Road club might wish otherwise, a line – if admittedly indirect - can be drawn between Hibs and Knox’s prowess in the ring.

“Before I got into bare knuckle, I boxed," he says. "But I was also fighting in football as well. I grew up in a place where there was a lot of gang culture, an environment of violence as a young boy. You had to be streetwise from a young age I suppose.”

He ran with the Capital City Service – Hibs casuals – from 17-years-old onwards. “I found it attractive,” he says. “It was something I felt I was missing: being part of a brotherhood, a group.”

The casuals scene, including rival groups such as ASC (Aberdeen Soccer Casuals) and Dundee Utility, seems to belong to another era of Scottish football. But the fights still happen, just further away from stadiums.

“Anywhere there isn’t cameras,” he says. “Back in the 80s and most of the 90s, you had groups of a hundred plus. Since TV took over, groups became smaller, more confined, more secret. You had to move with the times I suppose. You couldn’t wander around in groups of hundreds, you’d be seen by all the cameras.”

It became violence by appointment. “You’d phone and say: ‘Meet you there’. A set meet. Sometimes nothing would ever happen. You’d phone all day and nothing would happen. But you’d still have that day out with your mates.”

The arrangements could be painstaking. “It was all planned out. You needed management skills! A lot went into it. You didn’t just turn up and fight. What time were we fighting, what time were the trains, what pubs to go to? It was a lot of work. I could probably pass a management course now quite easily!”

Unlike some, Knox would always endeavour to go the game. He was and remains a football fan and played at a decent level. His first ambition was to be a professional footballer. He played for Hawick Royal Albert and Coldstream in the East of Scotland league – on the wing, wing-back or full-back and then, latterly, as a sweeper with a reputation for never shirking a tackle.

“I was still involved in the casuals scene, still attracted to it,” he says. “It was not all about violence. It was about being with your mates. We dressed the same, liked the same music. Away days having a laugh. It wasn’t all about fighting.”

But some of it undoubtedly was. He remembers once playing in a Scottish Junior Cup tie for Newcraighall, which had kicked off early. “I then went home and got changed before a fight with Raith Rovers, who were playing a Scottish Cup tie against Hibs,” he says.

“Everyone has got a bit older now. The scene has changed. Six guys v six guys, in a forest somewhere. Last team standing wins. To me that’s not football casuals, because you are away from everything.”

“I am not saying football violence is good,” he says. “But there’s so much more to it. It’s guys looking forward to being with their mates, they maybe need that at the end of the week. It’s a release. It acts as therapy for some people.”

The message is: don’t diss what you’ve never tried. The same could apply to bare-knuckle boxing, which is now edging into the mainstream to the extent that this weekend’s extravaganza has been advertised on the side of buses.

Maybe an invite onto the pitch at Hibs before a game might be forthcoming for Knox – it ought to be if he prevails this weekend, which would mean he is the No. 1 contender for the UK featherweight bare-knuckle title.

His ultimate dream is one likely to give Edinburgh city fathers pause. “My goal, my dream fight, if it wasn't Easter Road, would be on the castle esplanade,” he says. “Outdoors, in the summer. It would have a gladiatorial feel about it, you know? That would just be amazing.”

#1983. Parma vs Bologna - prediction, team news, lineups

By Jonathan O'Shea | 05 Nov 2026 16:44

One of Serie A's form sides, Bologna will aim to extend their success streak when they visit Emilian rivals Parma on Saturday evening.

While the resurgent Rossoblu have won three straight games before heading to Stadio Tardini, their hosts seem to be turning a corner too.

After being brought in during the last international break, Parma boss Alberto Gilardino experienced a tough start to life as their new head coach.

The club's second-highest Serie A scorer has a less stellar record in management, and he lost his first two matches after returning to the Tardini.

Yet, a gritty goalless draw with Udinese finally gave him something to build upon, before Parma beat an ailing Atalanta side on Monday night.

Rising star Simone Lontani notched the final goal in a stunning 3-0 away win, and that edged the Gialloblu out of the bottom three, with eight points from 10 games so far.

Having given their confidence a big shot in the arm, they can now anticipate the Derby dell'Emilia; and after February's 1-0 win, Parma will be seeking rare back-to-back victories over Bologna.

Of course, the visitors will have very different ideas, particularly as they have lost just one of their last seven league games at the Tardini.

Bologna also sit six points above their old foes in Serie A, due to a stunning run of results under new management.

Since Raffaele Palladino's arrival midway through September, only league leaders Lazio have picked up more points, and the Rossoblu recently posted their third win on the spin.

After beating Cagliari in Sardinia and conquering AC Milan at San Siro - the latter largely thanks to Samuel Mbangula's hat-trick - Palladino met up with his former club Monza.

It was far from plain sailing, as Bologna had to fight back from behind - and Lukasz Skorupski saved a penalty - but they finally got their first home win of the season.

In contrast to some dismal form at Stadio Dall'Ara, only Como have recorded more away wins in Serie A this calendar year, so they can certainly target maximum points in Parma.

The hosts will be without two potential starters on Saturday, as injury-prone midfielder Adrian Bernabe has suffered a thigh strain in training and young defender Dominik Drobnic has injured his left foot.

Abdoulaye Ndiaye is likely to replace the latter in Parma's back three, but it remains to be seen who starts in the final third.

Lontani's three Serie A goals have come from just four shots on target, and he is among several candidates to feature up front: El Bilal Toure leads a list also featuring David Romero, Nesta Elphege, Ousmane Diallo and Matija Frigan.

While Bologna's strikers have been very quiet this term, wingers Mbangula and Federico Bernardeschi have scored three goals apiece.

Furthermore, attacking left-back Juan Miranda has provided an assist in each of his last four matches.

Though Roberto Piccoli should be back in the Rossoblu's squad, they must travel without injured trio Lorenzo De Silvestri, Jay Enem and Emil Holm.

Daffara; Delprato, Troilo, Ndiaye; Britschgi, Fabbian, Sierro, Keita, Valeri; Lontani, Toure

Skorupski; Darmian, Casale, Theate; Zortea, Ferguson, Pobega, Miranda; Bernardeschi, Cambiaghi; Odgaard

Currently on 10 top-flight away wins this calendar year - already a club record with almost two months to go - Bologna will be dangerous opponents for Parma.

Now looking better organised and more potent up front, the visitors can claim maximum points from this regional derby.

#1982. Messi was a deity among Argentina’s unholy rabble

Little sorcerer calls time on playing for his country six weeks after World Cup final defeat which was marred by brutality of his team-mates

Oliver Brown leads coverage of the greatest events in sport all over the world. He has reported on multiple Olympic Games, World Cups, Ashes series and Super Bowls, plus all major golf and tennis tournaments. His awards include Sports Feature Writer of the Year and Sports Interviewer of the Year. He was named Sports Journalist of the Year in 2024 by the London Press Club. You can find him on X at @oliverbrown_tel.

Oliver Brown leads coverage of the greatest events in sport all over the world. He has reported on multiple Olympic Games, World Cups, Ashes series and Super Bowls, plus all major golf and tennis tournaments. His awards include Sports Feature Writer of the Year and Sports Interviewer of the Year. He was named Sports Journalist of the Year in 2024 by the London Press Club. You can find him on X at @oliverbrown_tel.

Lionel Messi’s haunted expression told you more than a three-page retirement statement, artfully displayed alongside a golden pen, ever could. Sobbing and desolate under a cloudless New Jersey sky, he understood that his last game for Argentina had also been among his worst.

Where four years earlier he had adorned the greatest World Cup final with two goals, he found no artistry to salvage this abomination of an encore, drifting into anonymity while his team-mates triggered a bare-knuckle brawl. No wonder he stood apart while Leandro Paredes and Nahuel Molina did their worst, preferring to absorb one more chorus of adoration from the blue-and-white disciples before forsaking the stage for good.

You could make the case that Messi, as captain of an unholy rabble that had sought only to kick lumps out of Spain, should have taken a moral lead by hauling his team-mates into line, rather than reducing himself to their level by agitating to have Marc Cucurella sent off.

And yet for 20 years, the little sorcerer stayed aloof from his nation’s most lurid antics on the pitch, establishing himself as a strangely beatific presence on whom the highest ideals could be projected. Anybody who has heard Messi’s name being chanted by 50,000 fervent Argentines would have felt it. He was as close as 21st-century sport has come to a secular deity, the object of such veneration that Pope Francis felt compelled to remind Catholics that it was sacrilegious to keep calling him God.

Today, with one agonised announcement, that glorious delirium is over, and already Argentina seems not to know what to do with itself. Pablo Giralt, a sports anchor in Buenos Aires, was unable even to speak when he heard the news live on air, while shattered young fans described how they had called their parents in tears.

Everybody had known the moment was approaching, given the finality of his exit from the final and the subsequent death of his father, Jorge, but it still triggered an unbearable sense of loss.

Messi was the force who galvanised a nation, propelling his side from the unfathomable low of defeat to Saudi Arabia at the 2022 World Cup to holding the trophy aloft 26 days later. Who could ever hope to emulate him, to detonate such joy that the team’s homecoming bus parade in the capital had to be abandoned for a helicopter ride because of the millions on the streets?

“Thank you, God, for making me Argentine,” Messi wrote in his earnest sign-off, his strength of allegiance unfailing to the end. As a veteran of 207 international matches, with his last at La Bombonera distinguished by an ecstatic ovation, he understood both the passions he unleashed among his people and the extent to which his own story became that of an entire country.

You struggled to imagine what life was like in the eye of this madness, with his every move stalked. For the wonder of Messi was that the cult went beyond borders, that the joy he inspired across six World Cups made him beloved to billions. An abiding memory of the 2022 final is of the walk back to the metro station in Doha, where thousands of Nepalese and Bangladeshi supporters, all part of the vast migrant workforce that had built the stadiums, united in “Messi, Messi” refrains even at 1am.

Messi was majestic at that tournament, so imperious in filleting Croatia in the semi-finals that Argentina’s TV reporters abandoned even the pretence of objectivity. “Truly, you made your mark in everyone’s life, and that to me is beyond winning any World Cup,” gushed Sofia Martinez of Television Publica. And when he won it all, the mark only deepened. To occupy any press box at the World Cup where Argentina were involved this summer was to see South American colleagues in “Messi 10” jerseys, helplessly in thrall to his greatness.

As a 39-year-old, he confounded every expectation, scoring a hat-trick against Algeria and breaking Miroslav Klose’s World Cup goals record. Even when engineering those implausible fightbacks against Egypt and England, he held a volatile team together with a minimum of fuss.

Lionel Messi: #FIFAWorldCup edition 🇦🇷🌟 pic.twitter.com/E2xOh3Iose

To study Messi at his last World Cup was to see a man spared the obligation to do anything off the ball. For large periods of each game, the most minutely scrutinised athlete on the planet would do little besides wander around, only to ignite when it mattered most. You saw it in the fateful semi-final with England, where, at 1-0 down, he sloped off to the right touchline as if absent-mindedly gardening. Except he was plotting his opponents’ downfall, working out the precise spots from which to unleash two sumptuous crosses and shatter English hearts.

That alchemy would elude him in the final, where Argentina’s bid for immortality brought only instant notoriety, not to mention £236,000 in fines for misconduct. Was Messi’s image hurt by his connection to the chaos? Not in the long run. Nobody likes to cling to the fact that Pelé’s swansong for Brazil was a drawn friendly with Yugoslavia, or that Diego Maradona bowed out of World Cup football by failing a drug test for ephedrine. What endure are the indelible masterpieces those players bequeathed en route.

It will be the same for Messi, a genius defined less by his ending than by the electrifying adrenalin rush he produced along the way, spanning three finals, 21 goals, and countless flourishes to take the breath away. “Thank you” was all he had left to say. And yet the gratitude, ultimately, is all ours.

#1981. Next Man United manager: Special Cesc Fabregas agreement truth 'revealed' amid Red Devils struggle

By Carter White | 05 Nov 2026 16:50, Last updated: 05 Nov 2026 20:51

Como president Miran Suwarso has denied the presence of a special clause in Cesc Fabregas's managerial contract.

Manchester United fans are watching the 39-year-old's coaching work with considerable envy at the beginning of this term, with the Red Devils supposedly reaching out to Didier Deschamps over potentially replacing Michael Carrick.

It is not only the dugout where the 20-time English champions are plotting change, with Man Utd keen to improve their defensive ranks in the New Year, leading to a supposed interest in Fulham and Nigeria centre-back Calvin Bassey.

Winning just one of their opening nine top-flight fixtures, Carrick's side are sitting in a lowly 17th position in the Premier League standings, lying outside of the division's relegation zone on goal difference.

Fabregas's up-and-coming Como outfit embarrassed Man Utd in the Champions League on October 21, when Argentinian ace Nico Paz bagged a brace in a 4-1 battering of the Red Devils in the League Phase.

Appearing on Piers Morgan Uncensored, Como president Suwarso discussed the future of head coach Fabregas, who has understandably attracted plenty of interest from other European clubs.

Reports in September suggested that the 39-year-old had a 'special agreement' in his contract that would allow him to depart the Serie A club to join three of his former sides - Barcelona, Arsenal or Chelsea - for a fixed compensation fee.

Como chief Suwarso has rubbished those rumours, saying: "He does not need a clause to go anywhere he wants. In a business like this, he is a friend more than anything else.

"He can go wherever he wants, whenever he wants. I could even say if tomorrow, he calls me and he says, 'Hey, I want to go to [Bayer] Leverkusen', for example. I would say, 'If that is something you want to do, then go'. I don't even need any compensation."

Fabregas's current contract at Como expires during the summer of 2028, before which intrigue in the young Spanish tactician is undoubtedly set to grow exponentially, including from clubs in the Premier League.

Given that it is down to Fabregas to decide the timing of his exit from Como, it is extremely unlikely that struggling Manchester United will be getting their claws on the Spaniard anytime soon.

The former Gunners midfielder is building something special at the Serie A newcomers, who could be the surprise package of the Champions League this term, following in the footsteps of Norwegian side Bodo/Glimt during 2025-26.

Man Utd are mess from the boardroom to the pitch at the moment, and nothing but the club's proud history stands above their competitors at present, leaving the Old Trafford faithful in relative misery.

#1979. Belief coursing through Eastbourne Borough veins – King’s revolution is moving fast

You have to hand it to Steve King. Less than eight months into the job that he has long coveted, he has won admiration as well as a lot of football matches, and he has simply transformed the mood at Priory Lane.

Back in the spring, supporters literally could not wait for last season to finish. Managers piling failure upon failure. Players arriving and departing before we had even ;earned their names - and a sense of malaise across the club.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

Now, the Sports are motoring - jostling for position at the head of a very competitive Isthmian Premier division. A long winter and demanding fixture schedules will test the mettle of all the leading clubs, and the simple policy at this stage is to stay with the pace-setters.

With a relentless Saturday-Tuesday-Saturday schedule, Steve takes his squad to North Kent tomorrow (Saturday) to face another of the contenders, Dartford. Realistically, the Sports will drop some points at some stage - but even when they do, Borough will not be knocked off course. Why? Because this Eastbourne squad is built on experience.

King's close-season business showed us the plan. The squad has been built around a core of players with massive experience at this level, and above.

Thirty-year-olds form the spine of the team, from goalkeeper through central defence and midfield, to wide players and strikers. Opponents glance at the team-sheet, and tremble. With names like Josh Rees, Darren McQueen, Liam Nash, Paul McCallum - they know they will be in for a tough ninety minutes.

And that team foundation also gives a platform for several gifted youngsters: Matt Hayden - wisely tied down with a new and longer contract - is proving one of the most exciting full-backs in non-league. Freddie Carter is a formidable presence. Arthur Grout is developing his sublime skills.

King's team-building is remarkable - and it is not random. The manager is - he will not mind the Herald saying it - a football obsessive. There is no such thing as a free evening in King's diary: he will be on the road to check out opponents, track player targets, catch up with the talk on the circuit.

If there were any doubters among the fans, those doubts are being dispelled. Last Saturday a huge crowd of over 1,750 revelled in a cracking contest with an excellent Ramsgate side - decided only in the last two minutes by two outstanding Shay Harrison strikes.

The smiles all round the ground, and the final-whistle roars, told their own story.

He's not the Messiah. But he's a very canny manager, and in a matter of months, he has transformed a football club.
