#1978. Simon Leslie: A brilliant Eastbourne Borough day for first-timers – and those who have been coming decades

That’s 14 wins from 15 games, and tomorrow we head to Dartford hoping to keep this extraordinary run going.

Saturday against Ramsgate had almost everything, although for a while it looked as though the one thing missing might be a goal. It was a fantastic, exciting game, but as the clock ticked down you started to think we might have to settle for a 0-0 draw.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

Shay Harrison clearly had other ideas. Two brilliant late goals later, Priory Lane was bouncing. If that was your first visit, I hope you enjoyed the finish as much as I did.

And for plenty of people, it was their first visit. Our friends at Octopus Energy gave tickets to local customers, and seeing the queues stretching out towards the street was a wonderful sight. So many new faces coming to see what their local football club is all about. Thank you to everyone at Octopus who helped make it happen. They certainly brought the energy!

Eastbourne did its bit too, with beautiful blue skies and autumn sunshine. The Octopus Energy fan zone was up, the children were playing and there were smiling faces everywhere. It was one of those afternoons when you could look around and think, yes, this is what we want football here to feel like.

There is something special about bringing someone to non-league football for the first time. You are so close to the action, you can hear the players and feel every tackle, every near miss and every decision you are convinced the referee has got wrong. Then a late goal goes in and suddenly you are celebrating with someone you had never met two hours earlier.

I really hope those who joined us for the first time will come back. Bring your friends, bring the children and make an afternoon of it. We want this to be somewhere you feel welcome, somewhere you enjoy spending time and a club you are proud to call your own.

Before kick-off, our Spirit of Football team paraded with the first trophy they had ever won. The children were absolutely delighted, and their excitement was one of the highlights of my day. Just imagine how much that moment meant to them, showing off their trophy in front of our biggest crowd of the season. A huge congratulations to everyone involved.

We spend plenty of time talking about results, league positions and what happens next, but seeing those happy faces reminds you how much a football club can mean to people. It was lovely to see them getting their moment and enjoying every second.

Then came Tuesday night, and Eastbourne’s blue skies had given way to wind and rain. A very different evening against Stanway Rovers, but the winning continued with a single-goal victory. Sometimes you get sunshine and spectacular late drama; on other occasions you have to dig in and get the job done. The boys found a way again.

Thank you to everyone who braved the weather to cheer them on. Fourteen wins from 15 games is some going, and the players and staff deserve enormous credit for putting that run together. We remain third in the league, with plenty of football still to play and plenty to look forward to.

Tomorrow we head to sunny Dartford - hopefully the weather will take the hint - looking to make it 15 wins from 16. Our away support has been terrific, and I know the boys will hear you again.

To everyone who came on Saturday, whether you have been coming for decades or were finding your way to Priory Lane for the very first time, thank you. I hope we will see you again soon. Shay cannot promise two late goals every week, but he has certainly given you a reason to come back.

#1977. The inside track on Celtic's squad spirit and pressure cooker every three days

Mika Baur is discovering that life at Celtic rarely offers a moment to catch your breath. The expectations are relentless, the schedule unforgiving and the emotional swings can be considerable.

But if Thursday’s crucial 3-2 Europa League comeback victory over Besiktas demonstrated anything, it is that there remains plenty of belief within the Celtic dressing room. After a difficult period, Martin O’Neill’s side retuned to winning ways by recording their first three points of the competition’s league phase at the fourth attempt.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

For German midfielder Baur, the result was particularly welcome after a bleak run of form. In a contest that demanded character as much as quality, Celtic found it through a blend of steely determination, attacking flair and the influence of their substitutes.

The 22-year-old believes the manner of the win over their Turkish opponents outlined Celtic’s ability to respond to adversity, although he recognises that life in Glasgow rarely offers time to dwell on either success or disappointment.

“The win was important after some tough weeks,” he declared. “But the belief and the way we work together as a team has always been good. There was never any problem with that because we always believed in ourselves. We showed how we can leave our hearts on the field and put in a shift. It was important to get those three points and we deserved it. Hopefully we can go forward with confidence from this game.”

The response to successive Premiership setbacks against Dundee United and Falkirk was particularly important given the standards expected at Celtic Park. Baur has quickly learned there is little room for inconsistency at a club where winning is a must at all costs, irrespective of the opposition or competition.

“There is always pressure to win here, to win every three days,” Baur admitted. “That’s what we all want. In the last two games it wasn’t possible for us. We knew it wasn’t good enough but here we played well and deserved it.

“The fans helped a lot. You could feel the energy. It was not just us players on the field who deserved the win – it was also everyone around the stadium and they brought the energy as well. It’s an unbelievable feeling as a player to have everyone pushing you and being there for you. It gives you that last percentage of energy you need at the end.

“Playing in this unbelievable stadium in front of these fans, you feel the pressure with some of the games we have lost but I am getting used to it. You don’t get much time.”

A decisive factor in Celtic's comeback was the game-changing contribution of Camilo Duran and Callum Osmand. Introduced from the bench, both players injected fresh energy into Celtic’s attack, helping turn the game in their favour, with the Colombian scoring twice and Osmand providing a goal and an assist.

Baur believes their performances underlined the importance of squad depth and the collective responsibility required to deliver success.

“That’s what you want from the subs – to make an impact from the bench,” he explained. “It says a lot for Camilo to accept the situation of starting on the bench, but to come on and make such an impact, producing in the big moments to score those two goals to win us the game. Ossie as well, he came on with a goal and assist. It’s not just the goals and assists, Ossie won the ball as well and was working hard. I’m really glad for them.”

#1976. How many points do Man Utd need in the Champions League?

By Naim Beneddra | 05 Nov 2026 17:01

Manchester United's dramatic comeback against Roma has revived their Champions League campaign, but Michael Carrick's side still have work to do to avoid an early European exit.

Tuesday's 3-2 victory at Old Trafford ended a nine-match winless run and lifted the Red Devils to 17th in the 36-team league standings, with six points from their opening four matches.

However, United are only two points above the elimination places at the halfway stage, having suffered consecutive defeats to Atletico Madrid and Como before their recovery against Roma.

With four fixtures remaining, including a daunting encounter with Bayern Munich, the question is how many more points Carrick's men need to secure a place in the knockout rounds.

The results of the previous two Champions League campaigns offer a useful indication, although the eventual qualification threshold will depend on how the other 35 teams perform.

Under the Champions League's expanded format, the top eight teams progress directly to the round of 16, while those finishing between ninth and 24th enter a two-legged knockout phase play-off.

The bottom 12 clubs are eliminated, with no opportunity to drop into the Europa League.

United currently occupy 17th place with six points, having recorded two victories and two defeats. Their goal difference stands at zero, with eight goals scored and eight conceded.

That places them inside the play-off positions for now, but offers little protection against further setbacks.

In the inaugural 36-team league phase in 2024-25, Club Brugge claimed the final play-off position with 11 points, finishing ahead of Dinamo Zagreb on goal difference.

The qualifying threshold was lower last season, when Benfica finished 24th with nine points, narrowly edging out Marseille on the same total.

Meanwhile, 16 points were enough to secure eighth place and direct qualification for the last 16 in both campaigns.

Those figures provide three possible targets for United.

A single additional victory would take Carrick's side to nine points, matching the lowest successful play-off total recorded under the current format.

However, that would not guarantee qualification, particularly given how tightly contested the lower positions are after four rounds.

Five more points would take United to 11, equalling the 2024-25 threshold, while two victories would leave them on 12.

Reaching 12 points would represent a considerably more encouraging position based on recent history, although even that total cannot be regarded as mathematically sufficient this season.

The task becomes substantially harder if United want to avoid the play-offs altogether.

To reach the 16-point benchmark, they would need another 10 points from a possible 12, meaning three victories and a draw, or four consecutive wins.

There is also an important distinction between qualifying for the play-offs and reaching the last 16.

Finishing anywhere from ninth to 24th would keep United in the competition, but they would still need to win a two-legged tie in February to progress.

For Carrick, securing a play-off place is therefore the more realistic immediate objective, with a top-eight finish requiring a near-perfect second half of the league phase.

United's remaining schedule offers opportunities to collect the points they need, although two of their opponents currently sit above them in the table.

Their next European assignment is a trip to Sporting CP on November 25, with the Portuguese side occupying 10th place on nine points.

The Red Devils then welcome RB Leipzig to Old Trafford on December 8, before hosting Bayern Munich on January 20 and concluding the league phase away to Villarreal on January 27.

Leipzig and Villarreal have each collected only three points from their opening four matches, making those encounters particularly important to United's qualification prospects.

Two victories against those opponents would take Carrick's side to 12 points, even if they failed to collect anything from their meetings with Sporting and Bayern.

That would have been enough to reach the play-offs in both previous editions, though United's final position this season would still depend on other results.

The Sporting fixture could also prove significant. A positive result in Lisbon would reduce the pressure on United ahead of their December home match and potentially strengthen their position against a direct rival for the knockout places.

Their January meeting with Bayern presents a different challenge, particularly given the German champions' attacking quality and European experience.

United's situation is also notably less comfortable than that of several other English clubs.

Arsenal have accumulated 10 points, while Aston Villa, Manchester City and Liverpool each have nine, leaving United as the lowest-ranked Premier League representative in the competition.

Elsewhere, Napoli sit 27th with three points, while Atletico Madrid and Roma are also in danger of missing out on the play-offs after collecting four points apiece.

For United, the victory over Roma has provided valuable breathing space, but the margin remains narrow.

Another six points would take them to 12, a total that has historically been sufficient to survive the league phase. Their next two matches, against Sporting and Leipzig, could therefore go a long way towards determining whether the Bayern encounter becomes a battle for qualification or an opportunity to chase a top-eight finish.

#1975. Two defeats won’t put Hastings United off-course – Dolan has strong belief in squad

United lost 1-0 in both Saturday’s clash with high-flying Faversham and Tuesday’s against lower-placed Deal Town.

The lack of points has seen them slip to fourth place, but they’re only two points behind leaders Whistable as they try to recover with tomorrow’s trip to Cray Valley PM.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

Dolan was disappointed with the losses but is not about to rip up his blueprint and start again.

Faversham won with a 30th minute spot-kick and United skipper Tom Chalmers was sent off in the final moments for two yellow cards.

Dolan said: “The Faversham game was a case of us giving them a little bit too much respect. They are a good team – well-organised – and are going to be there or thereabouts this season. And you can see why they are title favourites – they’ve got great experience and some great players for this level.

"But I think we turned up giving them too much respect from the get-go and that carried on through the whole game and we didn’t really test them like I know we could have done, or how we have tested other teams this season.

"That’s disappointing from us but we’ve been fantastic up until now so I’m not going to grumble after we’ve played a team who are near the top of the league and are favourites to win it.

"We were still in the game until the very end so we’re staying in games and not getting rolled over which is good. It’s one of those where you have to dust yourselves off and move on."

On Chalmers' red card, Dolan said: “I don’t really understand what he got the first yellow for. He was talking to the ref and the ref chucked a yellow out when they were wasting time. If your captain can’t talk to the ref, then who can?

"The second yellow I think was just frustration boiling over from him at the very end. He’ll be suspended on Saturday so we’ll make do without him.

"The Deal was game was very frustrating. As I said before that game, the league table doesn’t do them justice. They’re in a false position in my eyes – like Cray Valley, who we face on Saturday.

"Deal are a good team who have been at the level for a long time and have players who have been together a while. They’re very organised and they did a job on us – they had one shot on target in the 85th minute and it happened to be a goal. Whether we put that down to a lapse in concentration, or down to moments … this game was more down to fine margins.

"We had four or five really good attempts at goal but we need to be putting these chances away. It’s good we’re still creating chances but bad we’re not taking them. I’m positive over the fact we’re still creating them.

"Against Faversham we didn’t create much but against Faversham we created some good openings – we hit the post, had a one-on-one, their keeper made a great save and there were a couple of other chances. I’m happy we’re still creating."

Dolan is disappointed but not overly alarmed at the past two results.

"Our home form has taken a dip. In the FA Trophy game conditions played a part and in that game – like the Faversham – we gave them too much respect. And in the Deal game we dominated for 80 minutes then conceded a goal,” he said.

"Up until the Faversham game we’d scored in every game so I don’t put it down to anything in particular – it’s one of those things that happens in any football season.

"You’re not going to go along winning every game or scoring in every one, but I’m still positive and upbeat about what we’re doing. I’m fine with the team and the squad and everything we’re doing and how the boys are listening to what we want.

"Anyone who has consistency will do well – look at Whitstable with eight or so wins on the bounce and now they’re top.

"We’re a very young squad – and a new squad this season – so bits of naivety will set in and learning will be a part of it and it’s down to us to help each other through it, and pick out the moments where can do better it and rectify it."

The chance to do so comes at Cray Valley PM tomorrow. They sit 20th going into the weekend.

"The Cray Valley game is another against a team I think are in a false league position. On paper it looks a perfect chance for us to go and get back to winning ways, and I’d love nothing more than for us to go and win. But I also there’s players in their team who can hurt us if we’re not on our game,” Dolan said.

"There are some real threats in their team so we have to be at it from the beginning. We won’t take them lightly. Me, Sam (Adams) and Trevor (McCreadie) have discussed threats that they have and we’ll have reiterated that to the players and have a plan in place to try to go out and win the game. We have to be at our best and I’m sure if we are, we will win.”

#1974. Michael Carrick's next nightmare: How Aston Villa misfit Donyell Malen became Europe's hottest striker... as Roma star looks to pile on the misery for Man United in Champions League

Published: 02:00 EDT, 3 November 2026 | Updated: 04:31 EDT, 3 November 2026

It’s been a brutal start to the season for Manchester United, who are winless in nine games on the spin.

And as Michael Carrick fights to save his job, they must now find a way to deal with the most potent forward in Europe’s top five leagues.

Donyell Malen, the reinvented centre-forward, has caught fire in Italy, a world away from the talented but unspectacular winger who left Aston Villa.

The 27-year-old arrives at Old Trafford on Tuesday as Europe’s most prolific striker, with Roma unbeaten in Serie A. Villa let him go for just £25million.

Roma are contenders in Serie A, and Malen’s goals are the biggest reason why.

The Dutchman has totalled 22 goals in 2026. That is more than any player in the big five leagues, including newly crowned Ballon d’Or winner Harry Kane.

At Villa, it never quite happened for him. Malen arrived from Borussia Dortmund in January 2025 - the same window as Jhon Duran’s departure - but he spent most of his minutes out wide and never nailed down a starting place. Neither wing suited a player miscast as a pacey wideman.

Donyell Malen has scored 22 league goals in 2026 - more than even Harry Kane

Malen played just one and a half seasons at Villa Park, scoring 10 goals in 46 games

The Dutchman scored just 10 goals in 46 games at Villa Park, which hid his quality. He grew into his second season and was named Villa’s Player of the Month in November; but two months later, he was sold.

'It was my decision,' Malen told Italian media. 'I wanted to play and be part of a team where I could take the field every weekend and play an important role. At that stage, I didn’t feel important, so I think I made the best choice.

'Today I feel I’m in the right place with the right people. The coach and my teammates show a lot of confidence in me, and together, all of this is helping me become the player I dreamed of being.'

The signs of improvement were here before this summer's World Cup, though Malen  could not find the net despite starting all three Netherlands group games. Brian Brobbey was the side's focal point, returning Malen to a supporting role alongside Cody Gakpo.

It was a surprise to Dutch fans, who remember the centre forward terrorising defences at PSV, where he scored 19 goals and added eight assists in his final full season in 2020-21.

Roma boss Gian Piero Gasperini, who joined the club the previous summer, had moved Malen into a role he had not played in years: striker. The result was an outrageous 14 goals in 18 games to finish the season.

Malen has struck up a potent partnership with Paulo Dybala

Malen has rewarded his manager’s faith by helping secure Champions League football, a level the club have not reached since 2018.

Position is only part of the story. Once forced to create chances, Malen now finishes them. Argentine wizards Matias Soule and Paulo Dybala are his accomplices in a stellar front three, feeding him the best service in Europe.

Starting alongside Dybala, Malen got off to the perfect start to the season with a hat-trick in a 4-0 home win over Fiorentina.

'Getting off to such a good start by scoring a hat-trick was crucial,' he said. 'As a team we were strong and connected, and I immediately had a very good feeling. We can build on moments like these and do something special. Paulo and I clicked immediately.'

When Dybala’s constant niggles strike, new signing Rodrigo Mora has proved more than an adequate stand-in, helping to spearhead Roma’s title charge.

Gasperini has built a career on finding diamonds in the dirt. Alejandro ‘Papu’ Gómez, Josip Ilicic and Ademola Lookman all owe him a debt of gratitude.

Malen is not the only one from the Premier League’s discard pile to find new life in Serie A. Romelu Lukaku, Gianluca Scamacca, Scott McTominay and Rasmus Hojlund have all thrived there.

Even Tottenham flop Kolo Muani enjoyed an excellent six months in his first spell in Italy.

United's beleagured defence must find a way to stop Malen and avoid more humiliation

It hasn’t always worked - Evan Ferguson and Leon Bailey both disappointed at Roma - but it certainly has for Malen. Villa, meanwhile, can only watch. The sale allowed them to break roughly even, but it left supporters frustrated, with Duran, Moussa Diaby and Jacob Ramsey also sold in recent years.

It came as the club worked within the Premier League’s financial constraints.

Now Roma throw down the gauntlet at Old Trafford, and it could turn from bad to ugly for United.

'I don't think so much about the idol I'm becoming for the fans, I just want to score a lot of goals,' Malen said a few weeks ago. 'We have team goals to achieve and I'm focused on that.'

Malen’s eyes should light up against a volatile defence. A big night would push him further up the race for 2026-27’s top scorer and show English football the talent it only glimpsed.

The Seagulls should have scored when Rutter’s through-ball sent Hadjam racing clean through. Hadjam got to the ball before Soria but his finish clipped the keeper and came back off a post, with Yalcouye’s attempt from the rebound blocked on the line.

Azon threatened the Brighton goal again in first-half stoppage time but was once again denied by Verbruggen.

After the break some good build-up play from Rutter and Hadjam set up substitute Luka Vuskovic, but his shot was always curling away from the target.

The breakthrough arrived in the 64th minute when Pascal Gross lifted a diagonal ball towards the far post.

Overlapping full-back Costinha had acres of space on the right of the penalty area and cushioned his header back across goal.

Yalcouye’s timing was impeccable as he met the ball with a thumping header which flew past Soria and in off the crossbar.

Ibrahim Osman could have doubled the lead seconds after coming on but he could not make contact with Diego Gomez’s low cross.

Sunday, August 9, the words of Celtic assistant coach Shaun Maloney after watching striker Kasper Hogh score a 33-minute hat-trick in a 5-1 win over Kilmarnock.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Hogh had not long arrived at Celtic from Bodo/Glimt for £12 million, a record signing for the Scottish champions. His predatory instincts in Ayrshire led many to believe the Dane was on his way to the golden boot.

Fifteen games on for Celtic, Hogh has not scored a goal since. In fact, his manager Martin O’Neill is yet to see him find the net, as he was recovering from a “small procedure” for the match at Rugby Park.

Maybe the visit of Kilmarnock, who he terrorised on that summer’s afternoon, on Sunday will be the match where Hogh finally finds the net again. That is, of course, if the 25-year-old gets the nod in attack.

Hogh’s star is waning. The 25-year-old has been eclipsed by fellow July signing Camilo Duran, who has netted 13 times this season and clambered off the bench to help Celtic defeat Besiktas on Thursday night. The Colombian did more in his half-hour cameo than Hogh did in double that time. The poor hitman didn’t touch the ball once in the Turkish penalty box in the opening period.

It would be unfair to judge Hogh wholly on his goals, although at £4m per strike so far, that is an expensive outlay. Physical and hard-working, he offers Celtic a focal point. O’Neill was pleased with his performance against Besiktas. “I want centre-forwards to be able to hold it and that is what he did,” said the manager. “He is not Duran, he is not a dribbler. But if he can do this for us against strong opposition it will stand him in good stead.”

Hogh’s belief is bound to be low. How could it not be? He is out of the Denmark squad for the first time in over a year and when he tapped in from an already rescinded free-kick against Besiktas, there was a slightly sarcastic cheer from the home crowd. The misfiring forward is a real talking point.

“I think Thursday night will be good for him,” continued O’Neill. “I said to him that I’m not worried about whether he scores a goal. Of course you want centre-forwards to score and of course centre-forwards live on them. But I said to him that last night I wanted him to be strong and fight when the ball is played up to him. I thought in terms of holding the ball up and bringing people into the game that he did really well.

“Centre-forwards need a goal. But that performance there against European opposition will give him confidence. I don’t know what side we will play him on Sunday. But this lad has scored goals in the Champions League, remember. He will get a confidence boost from last night in terms of doing that part of the game well. But it will be nice for him to score a goal.”

The problem Hogh perhaps had is that O’Neill will turn to Duran more often than not now. “At this minute, he is on fire,” added O’Neill of the South American. “He can play wide right, he has done that. He has played wide left. But centre forward is where he is dynamic.” For now, unlike his strike partner.

#1971. Arsenal maintain perfect start but lack firepower of rivals

Bukayo Saka maintained Arsenal’s perfect start to the season, but Mikel Arteta appeared to acknowledge that the Premier League champions are in danger of leaving themselves short in attack.

There is still time for Arteta to add another forward to his squad and whether he does so or not could be important, with the transfer window closing on Tuesday night.

Having sold Leandro Trossard and with Gabriel Martinelli and Gabriel Jesus on the verge of moves away, Arsenal appear light of forward options.

Asked if he currently has enough depth in forward positions, Arteta added: “It depends if everybody is fit or not. We know that the depth has to be really big when you are fighting for four competitions. So we’re going to try to do that.”

0.52 - Arsenal faced the fewest shots (11), the fewest shots on target (1) and allowed their opponents the lowest xG (0.52) across the first two matchdays of the Premier League season.🔒 Locked. pic.twitter.com/blSUAeqoLb

Christos Tzolis is the lone attacking signing to date and there was evidence at Villa Park that it will be a risk to rely too heavily on the Greek winger.

Tzolis had made an exciting start to his Arsenal career in the Community Shield and the first Premier League victory over Coventry City, but he had to be taken off at half-time on Monday night.

The former Club Brugge winger not only lost out to Matty Cash, but was also at the centre of Villa appeals for him to be sent off.

Tzolis had already been booked for a foul on Cash, when, in the 36th minute, he appeared to foul John McGinn as Villa broke from the edge of their own penalty area.

McGinn appealed that Tzolis should have been shown a second yellow card, but referee Jarred Gillett let the Arsenal man off the hook.

Arteta was wise to take Tzolis off at the break and his replacement, Eberechi Eze, had a hand in what proved to be Arsenal’s 59th-minute winner.

Eze slipped in Riccardo Calafiori and Saka got in front of Ian Maatsen to poke the Arsenal full-back’s low cross into the net. Saka’s goal had been the first shot on target in the game.

"It's a brilliant goal, it really is" 👏 Bukayo Saka gives Arsenal the lead at Villa Park! pic.twitter.com/aV7DA8cARL

Just before the goal, Arsenal thought they had been awarded a penalty. Ross Barkley lost possession with a sloppy pass, allowing Declan Rice to advance towards the Villa penalty area. He played the ball through for Saka and Maatsen barged into the back of the winger.

Gillett paused before pointing to the spot, but a VAR check showed that Maatsen’s foul had taken place outside the penalty area and Martin Odegaard fired the resulting free-kick wide.

The goal and the overturned penalty were pretty much it for Arsenal in terms of threatening the hosts, for whom goalkeeper Zion Suzuki made his debut. Suzuki did not have much to do with his hands, but impressed with his distribution.

It was Villa who went closest to scoring in the first half, through one of the club’s five surviving members of last season’s Europa League-winning team.

Emiliano Buendia scored Villa’s second goal in the final against Freiburg and the Argentine rattled the Arsenal crossbar with a 20-yard shot that had beaten visiting goalkeeper David Raya.

Before then, McGinn had sent a shot over Raya’s bar and into the building site where Villa are redeveloping the club’s old North Stand.

Buendia, McGinn, Cash, Pau Torres and Victor Lindelof are the only Villa players to have started the Europa League final who have not left this summer.

Defender Ezri Konsa is one of Villa’s Europa League winners to have departed and he made his Arsenal debut as a late substitute. The defender received a mixed reception, as he was first booed by some home fans but was then applauded.

Other than hitting the bar in the opening 45 minutes, Villa squandered a chance for a quick reply to Arsenal’s opener when McGinn hesitated instead of shooting after being played in by Nicolas Jackson.

Jackson lasted 71 minutes for Villa in what proved to be a promising debut. In the first half, he raced away down the right before sending the ball across the six-yard box. But there was no team-mate on hand to convert.

One of Villa’s other summer signings, Alejandro Garnacho, is yet to make an impact for his new club. The Argentine got an earful from manager Unai Emery for not being ready to go on. He eventually replaced Ross Barkley, but could not help conjure an equaliser.

This is the start Arteta wanted. But, in attacking positions, Arsenal will finish the transfer window weaker than they started it if the club are not active in the final hours of the transfer window. And that could prove costly.

We lost. We competed well. They won the league last year. We are trying to build a team but a lot of positive things [beyond] the result. How we competed. How it was progressively better. We didn’t create clear chances. Some players made fantastic debuts. Suzuki and Jackson did very good work. I think it’s the first step forward and positive for the next matches.

Accepting this result, I think we had chances to draw the match but we are in our rebuild. It is the way [ahead for us] making these changes and I say to the supporters and players that the message is there in the way we played.

To lose one match is painful but after the pain we must try to get positive things, This is the reason I am optimistic. There are 38 matches we played two. We haven’t one point but we can get better hopefully. And we will get players [Mbaye and Harwood-Bellis].

We can feel confidence because how we want to build the team again is true, to compete like today.

I think the squad we have now is how we planned with the  players we wanted.

[Are you confident you have replaced the quality that has gone?] Yes.

I’m really happy. It’s a big win. It’s a tough place to come and earn the three points but I think we deserved it.

It was a game where 11 was not enough and the finishers came in and did a magnificent job to win it. I know how tough it is to win here.

Every big team struggles against them for the past four years because they are so good. They are well coached, have great players. Great in transition. The moment you lose the ball and let them run inside they are really dangerous but I love a lot of the things I saw from my team.

Ebs [Eze] creates the action that sees us win the game, Bruno with Mikel [Merino] in midfield changed the dynamic of it, Ezri [Konsa] really composed and calm with every decision he made and then Zubi… I’m really happy with all of them.

Every game in the Premier League it’s like [you’re saying] we have to win this game. We know the level. We know how difficult it is in this league.

[Can you sign Julian Alvarez tomorrow?] I don’t know. That’s for the people upstairs.

It was a very tough match. Aston Villa’s defensive setup made things difficult for us, constantly catching us offside. We couldn’t attack as comfortably as we did last week. But as you know, sometimes one goal is enough for us. We have a very strong defence.

Today, we were great out of possession too and didn’t allow transition attacks.

I keep my targets for myself. Every week I want to be there and try decide the game as that’s what I’m in the team to do. That’s my mentality.

[Have you seen Chelsea?] I’ve seen them. [What do you think?] We’ll see on Sunday.

Jamie Carragher explains how Arsenal broke Aston Villa down for their winning goal 🔎 pic.twitter.com/CAI8zhznrJ

Arsenal host Chelsea on Sunday at 4.30pm while Villa go to Hull City at 5.30pm on Saturday. It’s too early for a must-win game for Villa who showed some positive signs tonight but they could certainly do with one.

Arsenal win with a performance of efficiency and patience that emphasises their superiority when asked to grind out a result.

John McGinnis arguing the toss with the referee about his belief that he was fouled in the box in the dying seconds. It was outside the box and if Maatsen’s ‘tackle’ wasn’t a foul, neither was Gabriel’s.

Not sure the way of refereeing that lets a lot of calls go and waits for VAR is going to enhance the game.

Maatsen tackles Bruno Guimaraes in the Villa box with an ugly lunge in which he appears to scissor him, kicking his heel with one leg before knocking the ball away with the other but the referee deems it fair and VAR lets it pass, too.

Arsenal’s game management is working well as usual until Raya goes too long and the ball bounces through to Suzuki. But when he starts a counter-attack Alysson ends it with a dive and back come Arsenal.

Maatsen slides in late on Saka down the right, bypasses the ball and crashes into his shin. Yellow card.

Aston Villa probe but Arsenal hold them 30 yards from goal and when they do slide pass down the side of a defender for Buendia to chase, Bruno is ideally positioned to cover and make the block which he celebrates as if he were Leonardo Bonucci.

Eight minutes of stoppage time are signalled by the fourth official.

Suzuki races 15 yards outside his box to head a long pass away from Havertz to McGinn. Back come Arsenal after McGinn is squeezed off the ball but Wan-Bisska wins it back with a fine tackle. He is among the best one-on-one pure defenders in the league.

Zubimendi rattles Buendia’s bones in a crunching but legal tackle.

That was Rice’s last contribution as he limps off. He is probably OK but wise to withdraw him if he has had a twinge.

Maatsen drives down the left and cuts into the box. White leans into him, Rice guides him with a rigid left arm and the rampaging left-back loses his feet. Maatsen acknowledges Rice’s fine defending when he gets back up.

Quite a few outside observers questioned why Arsenal signed Konsa. This apparent injury to Mosquera is the reason. With Saliba out for months and Timber still struggling to regain his fitness, Mosquera was the only right-sided centre-back in the squad (unless they repurposed White, who is needed at right back).

Garnacho faces up Saka after being played down the left by Buendia but his cross is blocked by the goalscorer. Raya catches the resulting corner.

McGinn wipes out Merino from behind and is deservedly booked. Moments earlier Alysson was also booked for leaving one on Gabriel after the centre-half had cleared the ball, choosing not to put on the brakes and bodychecking him instead.

Unai Emery has just gone ballistic at substitute Alejandro Garnacho.

Emery clearly wasn’t happy with Garnacho not being ready to come on and let the Chelsea loanee know about it.

And Mosquera cannot continue having overstretched so it’s a debut for the former Villa stalwart who is greeted warmly.

Suzuki saves in a one-on-one with Havertz running through from 40 yards, waiting and refusing to go down and make things easy for Havertz, sticking up a right arm to block the shot. But he may have been offside which may mitiagte it in terms of not costing Arsenal anything but he really should have beaten the keeper.

Nice pass from Merino to set the hare running.

Barkley plays a diagonal pass across the turf out to Alysson on the right and he hares round Calafiori to cross from the byline but could not get the ball past Gabriel at the near post.

Now Maatsen goes flying but this time in the Arsenal box under a challenge from White that was a duplicate of the one 30 seconds before. ‘Premier League corrupt as f---,’ sing the Villa fans, ignoring the similarities between the two incidents. The defenders’ arms made contact with the attacking players but without the force to send them sprawling.

Havertz hits the deck in the Villa penalty area when challenged by Kamara as they fought for Odegaard’s scooped dink from the right.

Bruno Guimaraes and Mikel Merino are stripped and ready to come on.

Once again, it’s Riccardo Calafiori who opens up the opposition’s defence with his off-the-ball running. He is the one player in this Arsenal team who makes genuinely unpredictable and unexpected movements.

McGinn’s combination with Jackson looks promising and the centre-forward invites him to bullock forward down the inside-right channel with a clever pass but the Villa captain is soon swamped by yellow shirts and the ball gets stuck beneath his feet.

Gary Neville makes the fair point that one of Arsenal’s most unheralded qualities is their patience. Their confidence in their rock-solid defence does not make them reckless but they are always confident of finding a way. They trust the method implicitly.

Aston Villa 0 Arsenal 1 (Saka) Mosquera has the ball 25 yards out, left of centre, he strokes it to Eze who angles a pass to Calafiori running between Cash and Lindelof. He makes it to the byline and cuts back a low cross that Saka and Maatsen both lunge at and the Arsenal winger gets there first to turn it in.

"It's a brilliant goal, it really is" 👏 Bukayo Saka gives Arsenal the lead at Villa Park! pic.twitter.com/aV7DA8cARL

Rice, Eze and Odegaard stand over it. Rive walks away and Odegaard approaches the ball with a semi-circular run-up. He whips it over the wall and about a foot wide of the left post. Suzuki was stranded but no matter.

It was outside the box. Not all that sure it was a foul either. But Arsenal will have a free-kick.

Maatsen and Saka collide as they chase a Rice pass that Saka would never reach. Seemed to be outside the box.

It has been fairly dull fare so far as two systems and structures that cede little space clash.

Lindelof rises high to meet Rice;s dipping cross from the right as Havertz, on his shoulder, was poised to pounce. He heads it straight up and Suzuki leaps to catch it.

Now Barkley picks out a diagonal to send Jackson down the left. The centre-forward reaches the 18-yard line, cuts inside and works it over to McGinn who lofts a cross over Villa’s back-post runners and out of play.

Eze did his best work from the left last season. Villa start with Barkley scoop-chipping a pass from the middle out to the left, 40 yards upfield. Maatsen runs on to it and drives past White to ram a shot into the side-netting.

Arsenal were too slow to move the ball forward in that first half, and too loose with it when they did get into promising positions. There’s a lack of urgency in their passing. I wonder if we’ll see Bruno Guimarães soon… one of the reasons they signed him was to add more quick forward passing to their play.

Signs of encouragement for Villa without creating much while Arsenal have been stymied so far by Villa’s neutering of Tzolis and the left wing. Arsenal’s right-sided trio – White, Odegaard and Saka – look the most likely to create something.

Only a minute of added time to be played. Arsenal still lacking a spark, largely because there’s a lack of precision in their forward, line-breaking passing.

Villa will be very happy with this half. Much more like their old selves in terms of structure and organisation.

Calafiori’s throw to Gabriel is picked off by Jackson down the right and he dribbles down the right. He is forced to slow down to wait for a midfield runner. When Hemmings catches up, so have three Arsenal defenders and though Jackson bends in a low, cross to the edge of the six-yard box it is about 18 inches away from Hemmings’ reach.

Calafiori goes down in the Villa box when Pau Torres uses his arm to lever him away as they tracked the flight of a cross. The referee sees nothing wring in it and neither does VAR.

Gillett takes an age to stop the play when Cash uses his body to shove Tzolis over after the winger had played a pass. Cash obviously thinks he has rattled the new signing and is keen to rough him up some more. The ref does award a free-kick but only after that daft delay.

Tzolis loses the ball on the edge of the Villa penalty area, tackled by McGinn. The captain slots a straight pass up to Buendia who tries to bend a pass into Jackson’s stride as he sprinted down the inside right channel but Gabriel read the trajectory and got there first.

Suzuki picks out McGinn with a long pass. He feeds it to Buendia who gives Hemmings a chance to chase it down the left. Arsenal shuffle over in defence so he doubles back and returns the ball to Buendia. The No 10 whips over a dipping cross looking for Barkley and Jackson but Calafiori and Raya make sure the goalkeeper wins it.

We’ve not seen much from Christos Tzolis on Arsenal’s left wing so far. He’s been excellent since joining the club this summer but he’s hardly seen the ball in this opening half an hour and he’s just been booked after losing a battle with Matty Cash.

Arsenal free-kick 30 yards out, left of centre, for a foul on Lewis-Skelly who was artfully shielding the ball. Odegaard chips to the right post but Havertz heads it back across the box rather than going for goal and Villa clear.

Cash gets the better of Tzolis again in the tackle and then Suzuki sprays a perfect 60-yard pass out to Hemmings that Gary Neville, likening it to something Ederson was capable of delivering for Man City, one of the best goalkeeper passes he has ever seen. Tzolis was booked for stopping Cash running off with the ball.

Maatsen, who could never dislodge Digne for long, has a chance now to make the position his won. He strides down the left, exploiting Rice’s positioning error but his right-foot isn’t half as good as his left and his bending effort is scuffed far too straight and easily cleared.

Saka drives down the right after a neat Odegaard, Saka, White triangle. Pau Torres races over to toe the ball behind for a corner. Saka takes and Rice flicks it on at the near post and Suzuki tips it over. No corner, though, as Gabriel had rag-dolled McGinn at the back post after the Villa captain had backed in to him and tried to stop him making a run into the middle.

“Champions of Europe, you’ll never sing that.” Villa fans poke the wound.

Arsenal are finding it difficult to play through the middle of the pitch but have found Saka in space on the right wing on a few occasions already. Villa are congesting the central areas, where Odegaard does his best work.

Calafiori picks off Kamara’s pass looking, for the third or fourth time, to play someone, usually Jackson, in behind the left-back. A minute later Calafiori challenges McGinn for a bouncing, loose ball and stoops to use his head. colliding with McGinn’s boot. Was the head low or the boot high? Arsenal think the latter but the ref sides, rightly, with McGinn.

Arsenal corner on the left. The threat inherent every time Rice is in a quadrant diminished on this occasion because Mosquera barged Cash just after Rice struck the ball. Free-kick to Villa.

Timber may be preferred by Arteta at right-back but Saka prefers White. The two have a well-grooved partnership in tersm of who underlaps and who overlaps. They never seem to get in each other’s way.

Bukayo Saka does seem to be getting a lot of time and space on the right flank.

It’s looking a risky tactic by Villa at the moment as the England international is being invited to cut in towards the penalty area.

Havertz is played down the inside-right channel in the penalty area by a cute Odegaard pass bur he blazes his shot across goal and wide of the left post. A replay shows he was offside but even so it was a lazy finish.

Kamara grabs Tzolis round the waist from behind and when the winger hits the deck, rounds him and passus to Buendia who crashes a right-foot diagonal shot on to the bar from 20 yards. The ref did not see it as a foul despite Arsenal’s protestations but had it gone in it would have given VAR a dilemma.

Worth keeping an eye on Aston Villa midfielder George Hemmings tonight.

He is only a teenager and has emerged from Villa’s academy, but Unai Emery is already a huge fan.

Hemmings produced a highly promising performance in the Super Cup against Paris Saint-Germain earlier this month.

Suzuki misjudges the flight of Rice’s typically menacing corner and flaps at it but his defenders and an offside flag leave him without egg on his face.

McGinn stops Calafiori down the left then gives the ball straight to Tzolis. The Greece winger opens his body and passes to Lewis-Skelly who shoots with his right foot from the left of the 18-yard line. Cash slides in to block the shot and it loops over the bar for a corner.

Hemmings uses his strength to hold off Ben White and shift the ball inside to McGinn who wraps his left instep around a shot and wafts it into building site behind Raya’s goal.

Ibrahim Mbaye and Taylor Harwood-Bellis are in the directors’ box watching the game. Villa don’t look like a hastily assembled team.

Suzuki knocks the ball long with his left foot, looking for Jackson but the ball spins away from him to Raya who boots it back upfield. McGinn pounces on it, turns past Rice and plays Cash in down the right. He crosses towards the near post and Mosquera hooks it clear.

Arsenal kick off with Odegaard spinning and trying to play Saka in down the right as they defend the empty North Stand end. The ball skids off the turf and Saka can’t trap it. The ball goes out for a Villa throw-in.

Who dies in the summer and played for both clubs.

Arsenal are in fact in yellow and navy. My mistake.

Villa in claret and blue with a twist, the shorts are blue for the first time since, I think 2001. Arsenal are in yellow and black. Leeds, like Arsenal, have traditionally worn yellow and blue as their away strip but have been shunted into yellow and black as well by Adidas this season.

There are a few guys standing in the North Stand with hard hats on, and it appears they are on ball retrieval duty.

They will be on red alert for any wayward shots that land in the empty stand.

Warm reception for Ezri Konsa from Villa’s fans as he walked back to the tunnel with Arsenal’s substitutes.

Konsa joined Arsenal last week for £51m, ending a spell of seven years at Villa Park.

Wonder if the likes of Morgan Rogers and Emiliano Martinez will get a similar reception when they return here with Chelsea.

Aston Villa  Suzuki; Cash, Lindelof, Torres, Maatsen; Kamara, Barkley; McGinn, Buendía, Hemmings; Jackson. Substitutes  Bizot, Mings, Ruggeri, Garnacho, Abraham, Bogarde, Wan-Bissaka, Edward, Lynch.

Arsenal  Raya; White, Mosquera, Gabriel, Calafiori; Lewis-Skelly, Rice; Saka, Odegaard, Tzolis; Havertz. Substitutes  Arrizabalaga, Hincapié, Eze, Gyokeres, Konsa, Madueke, Merino, Zubimendi, Guimaraes.

Zion Suzuki is one of two debuts for Aston Villa tonight and there is a genuine buzz of excitement around the Japan international.

Suzuki was signed from Parma for £30m as the replacement for Emiliano Martinez and arrives with a stellar reputation.

He’s got big boots – and gloves – to fill, but Unai Emery is convinced he will become a future star at Villa Park.

The other debutant is record £65m signing Nicolas Jackson, who joined last week from Chelsea.

Good evening. Yes, the first match was not as planned but we must keep going forward. Today we are playing our first home match and I am looking forward. We need to try as soon as possible to get our best individuals fit for a good performance. And today is a good match for us. Ir is difficult but always with our supporters here we feel comfortable and confident. Hopefully we can transmit our positive energy to our supporters.

We lost the first game but it is not a [team full of rookies]. We have experienced players. They play with energy and know how we want to play. We have to adapt with Suzuki but we have confidence [in him]. Jackson, the striker, and other players, George Hemmings, he is young but played fantastically in pre-season. He knows how we want to play.

Today is a challenge but I’m really looking forward to how the players will respond collectively, individually. We know we are changing things but no excuses. We have to perform today, we have to try to adapt the new players, to build our team to get their best today.

I am positive and I am optimistic. The players are ready.

Aston Villa are in a transition period and rebuilding on and off the field.

Unai Emery’s 2.0 have been under construction all summer and there could be 10 new signings in by tomorrow morning.

Villa have of course lost six of the starting XI from last season’s Europa League final, with Morgan Rogers, Ollie Watkins, Ezri Konsa, Youri Tielemans, Emiliano Martinez and Lucas Digne all departing this summer.

The North Stand at Villa Park, which faces the iconic Holte End, is also under renovation and closed down for tonight’s game.

It could be a bit quieter tonight but there is still a mood of optimism among Villa fans, despite such a summer of change.

We have had a real block of training sessions to work on things and prepare for this game in the right way.

We will have time to make changes throughout the game [on why he has picked an unchanged team]. They did really well [against Coventry] and for the game we expect [tonight] they have the right qualities to hurt them and that’s how we start.

They have that [upheaval in personnel] but they have been with Unai for a long time, they are a super well-coached team and we know how tough it is always to come here. We are very conscious of that but also very ambitious.

That’s the way we want to play [with aggression] constantly from the first minute, to suffocate the opponent and be better than them.

[Does it being your 250th Arsenal Premier League game add something special to it?] Just to win [makes it special].

She wore… she wore… she wore a yellow ribbon …

Two changes – Zion Suzuki and Nicolas Jackson make debuts. Joao Gomes misses the match as the first of his three-game suspension and Marco Bizot drops to the bench.

Double debuts 🤩Your Villa XI to face Arsenal this evening 👋 pic.twitter.com/Zue0ZTSJt9

Arteta names unchanged starting XI but Bruno Guimaraes is fit for the bench. Ezri Konsa joins him there.

🟡 𝗧𝗘𝗔𝗠𝙉𝙀𝙒𝙎 🔵Unchanged for Monday night football 🔐🤝 Presented by @deel pic.twitter.com/ptvpKHDahn

In its rightful place 🏠🏆 pic.twitter.com/FMH4zve1aD

Good evening and welcome to live coverage of the Premier League match between Aston Villa and Arsenal from Villa Park. The champions travel to the team that finished fourth last season in buoyant mood and form despite some misgivings within their fanbase about their recruitment this summer.

It amounts so far to making Pier Hincapié‘s loan into a proper transfer, revamping the left wing with Christos Tzolis replacing Leandro Trossard and Gabriel Martinelli, upgrading options in central midfield by buying Bruno Guimarães and selling Cristian Norgaard – and signing Ezri Konsa from today’s opponents to give them the greatest elite defensive depth that I can recall at club since Manchester City’s Treble winners had Kyle Walker, Ruben Dias, John Stones, Nathan Aké, João Cancelo, Aymeric Laporte, Manuel Akanji, Rico Lewis and Sergio Gómez on the books at the same time.

Villa, by contrast, have endured a turbulent summer of trading with the departures of Europa League winners Morgan Rogers, Youri Tielemans, Lucas Digne, the aforementioned Konsa, Ollie Watkins and Emi Martínez, raising, along with other departures, more than £315m. They have spent about £180m to remodel the team though Johan Manzambi, who is injured, and João Gomes, who is suspended after his red card in the 4-0 defeat by Brighton, are absent tonight.

We can expect to see Zion Suzuki, Matteo Ruggeri and hopefully Nicolas Jackson and Leon Goretzka who have been registered in time to play, plus the loan signings Aaron Wan-Bissaka and Alejandro Garnacho. Still to come are the pending purchases of Taylor Harwood-Bellis and Ibrahim Mbaye in a process that emphasises how profoundly Villa are invested in and dependent upon their manager, Unai Emery.

After so much upheaval, it would be foolish to set much store on Villa’s 2-1 victory last season, sealed by Emi Buendía’s winner in the fifth minute of stoppage time. Arsenal barely broke sweat in blowing Man City away in the Community Shield and cakewalked to victory over Coventry in the league’s opening fixture. His past work suggests Emery will be able to forge another formidable side from his talented new squad but this match feels two months too soon for him against his old club.

#1970. Queens Park Rangers vs Lincoln City - prediction, team news, lineups

By Ben Sully | 05 Nov 2026 17:09, Last updated: 05 Nov 2026 17:10

Queens Park Rangers will face Lincoln City for the first time in 55 years when the two sides lock horns at Loftus Road on Saturday.

The R's are currently sitting in 11th place in the Championship table, while the visitors start the weekend in 19th position.

QPR may be one point adrift of the top eight, but they have found wins hard to come by over the last couple of months, having won just two of their last 10 matches.

The most recent of those victories came via an emphatic 5-0 scoreline against Swansea City, only to fall to a heavy 4-1 loss away to Southampton a week later.

Julien Stephan's side took a point from their latest outing against Burnley, with Jonathan Varane netting a second-half equaliser in a 1-1 draw at Loftus Road on Tuesday.

They should fancy their chances of picking up at least another point from Saturday's fixture, considering they have lost just one of their seven home league games this season (W3, D3).

A sturdy backline has helped provide the foundation for their strong home form, having conceded just six goals in their seven outings at Loftus Road, with only two teams letting in fewer on home turf.

While they have not faced Lincoln since 1971, QPR have won four of their previous six official meetings with the Imps (D1, L1).

Lincoln, meanwhile, are focusing on preserving their Championship status in their first season in the second tier since the 1960-61 season.

The Imps are currently sitting five points above the bottom three after winning four, drawing three and losing seven of their 14 Championship outings this season.

They have struggled to add to their points tally in recent times, having lost five of their previous seven matches, including their last two outings against Birmingham and Watford.

The Imps fell to a 3-1 home loss against Blues last weekend, before they were beaten by a narrow 1-0 scoreline in their midweek away clash against the Hornets.

As a result of Tuesday's loss, Chris Cohen and Tom Shaw's side have now gone three away games without a win since starting the Championship campaign with three consecutive victories on the road.

They have the league's joint third-best defensive away record with eight goals conceded, although they have netted just six times on their travels in the Championship this term.

QPR forward Alfie Jones will be out until the new year after sustaining a hamstring injury in the defeat to Southampton last weekend.

The R’s are also without the services of Amadou Mbengue, Tariq Lamptey, Nicolas Madsen and Rumarn Burrell, while there are doubts surrounding Jake Clarke-Salter’s availability.

Richard Kone, who has netted four goals in the last three games, is expected to be available for selection despite appearing to be forced off with a physical issue in the midweek draw with Burnley.

As for the Imps, they remain without the injured duo of Tendayi Darikwa and Mason Melia, while Conor McGrandles is a doubt after missing the last two matches.

Forward Ben House will drop out of the squad to serve a one-match ban after picking up his fifth yellow card of the Championship season in Tuesday’s defeat to Watford.

Lincoln are hopeful that Mikkel Ladefoged and Ethan Wheatley will prove their fitness in time for the trip to Loftus Road.

Queens Park Rangers possible starting lineup:

Charles; Adamson, Dunne, Edwards, Kemper; Poku, Varane, Kamara, Vale; Kone, Smyth

Wickens; Coubis, Elerewe, Bradley, Reach; Konak, Varfolomeev; Hackett, Street, Jefferies; Draper

QPR may not be in the best of form, but they have proven to be a tough team to beat on home turf this term, and considering Lincoln have lost five of their last seven matches, we think the signs points to a home win on Saturday.

Crawley Towns’ trip to Rotherham United has been postponed.

Their match at the the New York Stadium on Saturday, November 14, has been called off due to international call-ups.

Reds recently had two weekends off during the last International break due to call ups.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

#1968. Malick Yalcouye: The unlikely Brighton star nobody saw coming

Brighton spent more than £200m in the summer of 2024. Big names and established internationals arrived on the south coast but hidden among them was a £6m arrival from IFK Goteborg called Malick Yalcouye.

The Mali-born midfielder had made just 14 appearances for IFK but Tony Bloom's algorithms and data models must have been pinging notifications left, right centre - which is quite apt, as Yalcouye can play left, right and centre.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

The slightly-built 5ft 7in midfielder signed a five-year contract with Brighton and was immediately sent on loan to Sturm Graz.

He made 36 appearances for the Austrians -including eight in the Champions League - and scored four goals with two assists.

It was a solid seasons work and the next step was the second tier of English football and a loan move to Swansea.

Alan Sheehan was the head coach at the start of the season for the Swans but he was replaced by Vitor Matos, who was the elite development coach at Liverpool under Jürgen Klopp.

Yalcouye totalled 36 outings for Swansea and helped them to an 11th placed finish but it's fair to say the Brighton man had a mixed loan spell in south Wales.

His performances did little to suggest he would be such a force for Brighton in the Premier League or Conference League this season.

But the Seagulls have been here before. Yasin Ayari under-performed while on loan at Blackburn and Coventry - in fact the Sweden international described his stint at Coventry as "total shit" but he is now a machine in the Premier League for Brighton and a potential £60m-plus player.

Yalcouye, 20, probably isn't as harsh as Ayari in his assessment from his season in the Championship but his start to the current campaign has taken his career to a new level.

He has featured in every match in all competitions so far. He has played every minute of the Conference League phase and started both Carabao Cup matches away at Manchester United and Manchester City.

He has started three in the Premier League and scored in two of those - both of which were excellent goals at Chelsea and Coventry.

He also scored in the Carabao at City and netted a powerful header in Brighton's 1-0 Conference League win at Getafe last night.

Albion boss Fabian Hurzeler, speaking after Thursday night's win at the Estadio Coliseum, said: “Malick has different skills and one skill is that he can attack the box well.

"He didn't only show it today or prove it today. He proved it through the whole season."

Yalcouye's stature and running power has drawn comparisons with former Leicester, Chelsea and France midfielder N'golo Kante but Yalcouye is different.

He can play the deeper midfield role but using him in advanced positions is a very clever move from Hurzeler and that's what has taken many by surprise.

Brighton's attacking players have to defend and press relentlessly high up the pitch and few players do that as well Yalcouye.

At first you think he's in the team for his running power alone. Then you realise, actually he's technically pretty good as well. He's also calm in front of goal and for a small player he can header with the best of them - his excellent goal at Getafe was case in point.

But surely his slight physic is going to be a problem when it comes to one-one duels in Premier League? Nope.

"Everyone looks at him and thinks he's too small," said Brighton skipper Lewis Dunk to Sussex World.

Dunk also stated that Yalcouye is "shy" lad but the squad are helping him grow in confidence and develop, which is what Brighton do best.

Yalcouye is one of the best stories to emerge from Brighton this season. He's a unique talent and has made it to the top level against the odds... and with a little help from Bloom’s data model.

His contract runs until 2029 and no doubt Brighton are already looking at that and considering improved terms.

Yalcouye's £6m arrival in 2024 went beneath the radar, but not anymore. He has a huge role to play as Brighton look to achieve something special this season.

Aiming to record three consecutive successes at their Highbury Stadium fortress, Fleetwood Town host fellow League Two outfit Rochdale for a clash in the first round of the FA Cup on Saturday afternoon.

The Cod Army have taken Arsenal's scalp on home soil in recent times in the EFL Cup, whilst the Dale are struggling to get a grip on the fourth tier following their promotion from the National League.

Despite mulling around in the lower reaches of the League Two standings since their League One relegation in 2024, Fleetwood Town have enjoyed the spotlight recently after a historic cup success.

On October 27, the Cod Army welcomed Premier League champions Arsenal to Highbury and knocked their visitors out of the EFL Cup, with the hosts earning a quarter-final tie with Everton in the middle of December.

Scoring in both the beating of the Gunners and last weekend's 3-1 third-tier victory over Bristol Rovers, Aaron Loupalo-Bi is experiencing a breakthrough campaign in senior football, with the Fulham loanee netting five competitive goals for Fleetwood so far.

Captaining Rochdale at the age of 41 earlier in the week, Ian Henderson should keep his spot at the focal point of attack.

That being said, the Dale will be keen to get Derby County loanee Brown back into the starting XI for a winner-takes-all clash at Highbury.

#1966. Inside Oliver Glasner's Forest struggles: Unserious players who act like superstars when they don't deserve to, alarming physical data - and squad's grumbles revealed

Published: 12:00 EDT, 2 November 2026 | Updated: 05:17 EDT, 3 November 2026

If football management were gambling, Oliver Glasner has just done the equivalent of walking into one of Nottingham’s top casinos and chucking everything on red.

Not satisfied with hammering his Forest players publicly after Saturday’s 2-0 defeat at Brentford, Glasner then had the squad running on the banks of the River Trent for their customary Sunday recovery session. The social media footage has to be seen to be believed – Premier League footballers jogging through an overgrown field, filmed by a baffled dog-walker.

Even if Forest were doing well and their players were easy to manage, these would still be risky moves. Instead, Glasner's side are 19th in the table and he is trying to handle a notoriously restless dressing room.

Forest are believed to pay Glasner more than £10million a year and until now owner Evangelos Marinakis has been patient. But in the Premier League most fans are sceptical when club officials talk about long-term projects and three-year plans. Only three of the current 20 managers have lasted three years in their current job.

Any manager who loses regularly is under pressure, particularly at a club who sacked three managers last season and another in the summer. Glasner has lost six of 10 as Forest boss and won only once. Forget the spin: results alone mean Glasner is under the pump.

If there are no signs of a reaction against Manchester City on Saturday, it promises to be an uncomfortable November international break.

If there are no signs of a Nottingham Forest reaction against Man City on Saturday, it promises to be an uncomfortable November international break for Oliver Glasner

There was not one single moment that broke Glasner’s patience but the 30th minute at Brentford on Saturday probably contributed heavily.

Forest centre back Murillo, who has regressed alarmingly this season, watched idly as Bees goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher launched the ball way over his head and into the path of Dango Ouattara. Ouattara then breezed past Murillo before Nikola Milenkovic turned the cross into his own net. Glasner was unhappy with the shape Murillo was in when he returned for pre-season training and was furious at such slack work.

It was not the first time Forest had been exposed like this, either. Jay Dasilva’s winner for Coventry at the City Ground in September came from a similar diagonal pass from keeper Carl Rushworth, though that time Daniel Munoz – one of Glasner’s pupils – was at fault. Again, slack. Again, sloppy.

Daily Mail Sport understands Glasner does not see enough seriousness in his squad. This group of players get on well but nonetheless, there is a view that poor results do not hurt them enough. Is it really time for laughing and joking around the training ground when you have taken one point from a possible 15?

Most of this squad have never won a European trophy, or one in Europe’s top five leagues. Glasner has three. Some around him believe there are Forest players who carry themselves like superstars when they do not deserve to.

It is thought Glasner is also frustrated with himself. Looking back, perhaps he wishes he had started with a bang, because the 52-year-old was alarmed at the physical data from previous seasons.

In 2024-25, Forest covered fewer kilometres than any other team, and last season only Liverpool and Chelsea covered fewer. In 2024-25, only Arsenal made fewer sprints; last season, only Everton were below Forest. Glasner’s Palace sides were never lower than 12th in those four categories.

When Glasner has been outspoken in the past, it has usually worked. At Wolfsburg and Frankfurt, performances improved. At Crystal Palace last season, Glasner let rip at his bosses after a game at Sunderland last January and most expected him to be sacked. Instead, he left in the summer after delivering the Conference League. The dynamic at Forest is very different though – and Glasner may soon understand why.

Glasner was unhappy with the shape Murillo (left) was in when he returned for pre-season training and was furious at the Brazilian's slack work at Brentford

Player power was a major factor in Ange Postecoglou and Sean Dyche's sackings last season. When players believe they can go above the manager’s head and vent to those in charge, they will. This is the danger for Glasner.

Daily Mail Sport understands there are players who love neither the new style – Glasner is a committed three-at-the-back man and many of the squad feel more comfortable in a back-four – nor the Austrian’s strict approach. He is very different from the avuncular Vitor Pereira, whose easy charm and light-touch approach united the squad post-Dyche and kept Forest in the top flight.

Others are surprised Glasner has not made it a priority to bring the dressing room’s strongest characters onside. Along with Morgan Gibbs-White, both Ola Aina and Callum Hudson-Odoi are powerful voices in the squad and alienating any of them is dangerous. Equally, Ibrahim Sangare and Nico Dominguez are well-respected, and both have been left on the fringes like Aina and Hudson-Odoi.

While Gibbs-White is clearly Forest’s best player, he can be a complex character. If the skipper is not 'having’ a Forest manager, his position becomes vulnerable.

It was a turbulent summer for Gibbs-White, who was frustrated no Champions League club came in for him and ultimately changed agents. He was also left out of England’s World Cup squad. Some believe that Glasner’s rigid tactical framework does not bring the best from Gibbs-White, who likes to roam across the front line and drop deep when he wishes. While Pereira understood this, Glasner does not operate like that.

At times this season, Gibbs-White’s body language has been striking. Team-mates who make mistakes feel his anger but the 26-year-old has only one goal (a penalty) and two assists this term.

Gibbs-White watched team-mate Elliot Anderson leave Forest for City last summer and perhaps questioned why he was not on the same path to the Champions League.

It is tempting to wonder about some of the advice Gibbs-White has received from those around him, though. Because if Gibbs-White is wondering why he is still playing for a bottom-half Premier League club, it is never a bad idea to look in the mirror.

Callum Hudson-Odoi is a powerful voice in the dressing room and Glasner would do well not to isolate him

If  Morgan Gibbs-White is wondering why he is still playing for a bottom-half Premier League club, it is never a bad idea to look in the mirror

Marinakis did not make Glasner the highest-paid manager in Forest’s history just to show him the door at the first sign of trouble. When the pair held talks, Glasner is thought to have stressed the need for time to make his vision work.

Neither man suffers fools and it is easy to imagine that Marinakis would have approved of parts of Glasner’s outburst. That does not give Glasner a free pass, because Marinakis factored in player feeling when dismissing Postecoglou and Dyche.

If the Glasner experiment fails, George Syrianos will come under scrutiny. Forest’s chief football officer has more power at the club than at any other time and he pushed hard for Glasner, whom he has known for some time through links to German football.

It is believed the pair had some contact over possible transfer business during Glasner’s time at Palace, and Glasner would likely have welcomed the chance to work with Syrianos at Selhurst Park.

In December 2023, Syrianos wanted Glasner to replace Steve Cooper but Marinakis chose Nuno Espirito Santo instead. Marinakis’ son, Miltiadis, is at the training ground regularly and will report back to his father. These are testing times for Glasner and his champion.

Dyche has had his say, too. During a poor run of results last season, he gathered the Forest players and staff for their views on what needed to change.

Anticipating their opinions on formations and tactics, Dyche was bewildered when one player queried the decision to move the weekly barber visit from Friday to Thursday. Nevertheless, that player is still at Forest and Dyche lasted less than four months.

Dyche  made many mistakes at Forest but his latest posts on Threads felt relevant.

If the Glasner experiment fails, George Syrianos will come under scrutiny. Forest’s chief football officer has more power at the club than ever before and he pushed hard for Glasner

The problem at Forest is that even if the players fail to stand up and be counted, they are rarely the ones to pay the ultimate price

They read: ‘The badge is bigger than all… and yet it seems not nowadays! I can only hope it turns and the culture we were insisting upon is now being assessed and realised as what was and is needed. Oliver is out there saying what I was saying… in his own style.

‘Nottingham Forest are still finding the goals hard to come by – and I had it along with my staff – we scored but nowhere near what the metrics were telling us, so not enough to stay in our job?

'We had 35 efforts at goal v Wolves and yet a 0-0 result and it culminated in myself and staff being sacked. I hope Oliver is given more time, the fans stay with him and the players stand up and be counted.'

The problem at Forest is that even if the players fail to do so, they are rarely the ones to pay the ultimate price.

"Like the performance the other day, you can see everyone was digging in for each other and we were fighting together. And we had a man sent off very, very early on in the game as well."

"I've only got positive things to say about him. He helped me a lot. He was able to push my career and my playing style onto another level.

#1964. Steyning Town edged out by AFC Croydon Athletic in thriller

The sides were separated by just two points in the table and the Barrowmen headed into the fixture full of confidence following an impressive 2-0 victory over Sittingbourne in their previous outing.

The opening ten minutes proved to be a fairly even contest, with neither side able to establish control.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

The first meaningful opportunity did not arrive until the 18th minute, when James Taylor tried his luck from outside the box. However, his effort was comfortably gathered by Steyning goalkeeper Alfie Mansell.

Steyning continued to struggle to create any real attacking threat. Croydon began to find more opportunities, with Jayden Raymond testing Mansell in the 24th minute. The Steyning keeper pushed the ball behind for a corner.

That brought further danger for the hosts, but Harvey Woolard produced an important goal-line clearance. Steyning looked to respond four minutes later from a corner, but Croydon keeper Amaadou Tangarn was on hand to punch the delivery clear.

Croydon continued to threaten, with Luke Dreher trying his luck in the 34th minute. Once again, Mansell was equal to the effort.

The hosts finally managed to register a shot on target in the 38th minute as Ryan Worrall struck a low effort towards goal, but his attempt drifted wide.

And Steyning’s resistance was broken just two minutes later. Raymond found himself unmarked and made no mistake, driving a low effort into the bottom corner to give Croydon the lead.

Things quickly went from bad to worse for Steyning as Raymond struck again in the 42nd minute. The forward was perfectly positioned to turn home a close-range tap-in, doubling Croydon’s advantage and leaving the hosts with an uphill battle.

Steyning attempted to find a response before the break, with Jesse Sentamu sending an effort over the crossbar in the 45th minute. Another opportunity followed from a corner but the resulting header also sailed over.

Steyning returned for the second half looking to turn the game around, but once again made a slow start, struggling to find a way through Croydon’s organised defensive line.

The hosts eventually found a breakthrough in the 61st minute. A deflected cross earned Steyning a corner, and following a scramble inside the area, substitute Max Blencowe managed to find the back of the net to make it 2-1.

Croydon continued to hold their defensive shape and limit Steyning’s opportunities. A free-kick for the hosts in the 66th minute was comfortably caught by goalkeeper Amaadou Tangarn, before James Taylor delivered a dangerous cross a minute later.

The Croydon defence could only spoon the ball behind for another corner, but Steyning were unable to make anything of the resulting set-piece.

However, the momentum was beginning to shift. Just two minutes later, substitute Alex Brewer produced a moment of real quality, striking a beautiful effort from outside the box to level the scores at 2-2 and complete an impressive comeback.

Mansell was called into action twice in quick succession, producing two important saves to keep Steyning level and prevent Croydon from immediately restoring their advantage.

But the visitors were not prepared to settle for a point. In the 77th minute, Josh Williams produced a brilliant finish to put Croydon back in front at 3-2.

Steyning pushed hard for another equaliser in the closing stages, but Croydon remained disciplined at the back, quickly closing down space and preventing the hosts from delivering the ball into dangerous areas.

A late opportunity arrived in the 88th minute, with Blencowe looking to grab his second, but his effort was comfortably dealt with by Tangarn. Brewer then came close to finding another late goal in the 90th minute, only to send his effort over the crossbar.

Croydon’s Noah Watson received a yellow card in the 94th minute for time-wasting as Steyning struggled to maintain possession during the closing moments. The hosts earned one final corner in the 95th minute after another effort went wide, but the set-piece came to nothing.

The final whistle confirmed a frustrating 3-2 defeat for Steyning, who had shown tremendous character to fight back from two goals down and restore parity, only for Williams’ late intervention to deny them a share of the points.

Steyning are 15th and host Horley Town on Saturday.
